The trailing-punctuation trim here strips only `. , ; : ! ?` (TRAILING_PUNCTUATION at line 10) and an unbalanced `)` (line 44). A link wrapped in double quotes in prose or terminal output, `"ao://sessions/proj/sess"`, matches via the greedy `\S+` with the closing `"` retained, and parseSessionLink then accepts sessionId `sess"` as valid. The link renders but resolves to nothing, so the user sees "That session is missing or is not accessible" instead of navigation. The same happens for `]`, `'`, `»`, and `>` as closing delimiters. Confirmed with findSessionLinks('"ao://sessions/proj/sess"') returning text `ao://sessions/proj/sess"`. Consider stripping a matching wrapping delimiter (quote/bracket) the same way the unbalanced `)` is handled.

The empty-segment guard checks `segment.length === 0` before decode, and the truthiness check at line 19 runs after decode, but a decoded `" "` is truthy. So `parseSessionLink("ao://sessions/%20/%20")` returns `{ projectId: " ", sessionId: " " }`. Harmless in practice since resolution then fails and the missing-session error fires, but a parser advertised as strict should reject whitespace-only ids. Trimming and re-checking emptiness after decodeURIComponent would close it.

RAW_SESSION_LINK is greedy to the next whitespace, so `ao://sessions/p/s/` and `ao://sessions/p/s/extra` both match, fail the two-segment rule at line 16, and linkify nothing (findSessionLinks returns []). This is arguably the correct treatment of malformed input, and prompt-compliant agent output is always exactly two segments, so impact is low. Flagging it because a single stray trailing slash renders the whole link as inert text rather than surfacing any feedback.

**Medium — Final crash output can be dropped.** This closes the logger on the child's `exit` event, when stdout/stderr may still have buffered output to deliver. Subsequent data callbacks call `writeDaemonLog()` with no active stream and silently discard those chunks, potentially losing the end of the panic stack. Node explicitly documents that stdio may still be open at `exit`: https://nodejs.org/api/child_process.html#event-exit. Please finalize logging on child `close` instead, using a logger owned by that child so an intervening restart cannot mix output or close the replacement logger. A regression test should deliver stderr after `exit` but before `close` and verify it precedes the exit marker in the file.

**Medium — An old stream's error can disable the replacement logger.** Rotation/restart calls `end()` on the previous stream and immediately assigns a new stream. The previous stream can still emit an asynchronous error while flushing; its handler then unconditionally clears `daemonLogStream`, disabling the healthy replacement and silently dropping subsequent output. Please capture the stream in this handler and clear the shared reference only if it still points to that same stream. Add coverage that opens a replacement, emits an error from the old stream, and verifies subsequent writes still reach the replacement.

**Changing only the model or mode cancels a running review without the confirmation.**

`chooseModel` calls `saveReviewer` directly. Only `chooseReviewer` goes through `reviewerSwitchWarning`. On the backend, `SwitchReviewer` sees the same harness with a different config and calls `resetReviewerRuntimeLocked`. That destroys the live reviewer pane and clears `AgentSessionID` before relaunching.

I reproduced this with a Go test against this head. The fixture is the same as `TestSwitchReviewerRestartsLivePaneWhenOnlyConfigChanges` except the run is `running`. Calling `SwitchReviewer(..., ReviewerCodex, AgentConfig{Model: "gpt-new"})` destroyed `codex-pane`, and the run ended `failed` with `reviewer native conversation was unavailable during restore; retry the review`.

Suggest running the model/mode change through the same warning as a reviewer switch.

`running` is the route param captured when the review screen pushed this sheet (`running: String(anyReviewRunning)`). `load()` fetches fresh `reviewState` but never re-derives it. So if a review starts while the sheet is open (for example an auto review on a new commit), switching reviewers cancels it with no warning.

Consider deriving it from the loaded state, e.g. `reviews?.reviews.some((r) => r.status === "running")`, and refetching before deciding whether to warn.

**The "Automatic review failed" banner never dismisses itself.**

This effect depends on the `autoReviewFailure` object. The banner only shows when `autoReviewEnabled` is true, and in that case the interval below calls `load(true)` every 2s. Each call parses fresh JSON and calls `setData`, so `latestAutoReviewFailure` returns a new object. The effect re-runs and resets the 10s timer before it can fire.

I reproduced this in React 19 + jsdom with this exact effect and polling. The banner was still visible at 15s. The same code keyed on `autoReviewFailure?.id` cleared at 10s.

```suggestion
	}, [autoReviewFailure?.id, dismissedAutoFailureId]);
```

(The effect body should also read the id into a local so the lint rule stays happy.)

**This fallback can pick the wrong PR (edge case).**

`/sessions/{id}/pr` (`ListPRSummaries`) merges PR alias rows (repo transfer or rename, or different URL forms of the same PR) into one summary keyed on the newest row's URL. The review list (`Plan(prs, runs)`) keeps one entry per raw row. The new review notifications deep-link with the raw `run.PRURL` (`emitReviewNotification`). If that URL belongs to an older alias row, this lookup misses and falls back to `prs[0]`.

With a single PR that's harmless, because it's the same logical PR. If the session has more than one PR, resolve, re-request review and send-to-worker act on a different PR on GitHub.

Suggest showing a "PR not found" state instead of `?? prs[0]`, or matching by repo and number.

**High: TUI (and non-async Chat) sessions stay in `provisioning` forever.**

`seed.ProvisionState = SessionProvisionProvisioning` is set whenever a preparation token is claimed, but only `completeAsyncChatSpawn` ever moves it to ready. The frontend sends `taskPreparation` for every mode, and `DelegateTask` ignores `Async` for TUI, so a TUI task spawns synchronously and its row stays `provisioning`:
- The board shows "Starting…" forever.
- `reconcileLive` skips the session.
- On the next daemon restart, `FailInterruptedProvisioning` marks this *working* session as failed.

The same happens for a Chat task when `m.chat == nil`, because that also takes the synchronous path. Suggest setting `provisioning` only when the async Chat path will actually run, or marking ready at the end of the synchronous spawn.

**High: a leftover preparation row can stop the daemon from starting.**

`CleanupInterruptedTaskPreparations` runs inside `ReconcileStartupSafety`, and daemon.go aborts startup on error ("reconcile sessions on boot"). A row with a branch but no workspace path is common: any preparation still running at a normal shutdown ends up that way, because the cancelled context makes worktree creation fail. On the next boot, cleanup calls `loadProject` and then `createSessionWorkspace`, building a worktree just to delete it. If the project was removed, the repo moved, or git fails transiently, the error propagates and the daemon refuses to start on every later launch.

Suggest making cleanup best-effort (log and drop the row) rather than returning the error, and not creating a worktree only to tear it down.

**Medium: attachments staged in a short window can go missing.**

`restoreAttachments` runs before `SetSessionProvisionedWorkspace` (line 181) records the worktree path. A `StageAttachments` call in that window still sees an empty `WorkspacePath` and state `provisioning`, so it only writes the saved copy via `PutCanonical`. Nothing copies that file into the worktree afterwards, yet the queued message that refers to `.ao-attachments/...` is still delivered, so the agent gets a path that doesn't exist.

Suggest recording the workspace path first, then restoring attachments (or restoring once more after recording it).

**Medium: killing a session during provisioning leaves it showing "Starting" forever.**

`Kill` calls `cancelAsyncChatSpawn` first. The `ctx.Err()` exits here and at lines ~189/201 clean up the worktree and return without changing `ProvisionState`. The row ends up terminated but still `provisioning`, and `FailInterruptedProvisioning` skips terminated rows, so nothing ever corrects it. `SessionsBoardAdapters.tsx:49` gives `provisionState === "provisioning"` priority over terminated, so the board keeps showing a pulsing "Starting Codex…". If the session is later restored, `Send` keeps routing messages to the no-controller queue.

Suggest setting a terminal provision state (failed or cancelled) on the cancellation exits as well.

**Medium: a session that failed to start has no way forward.**

With `provisionState === "failed"`, the controller reports `stopped`, so the composer is disabled, and `!starting && controller.state === "stopped"` hides Resume and Open shell. On the backend, `Send` refuses because there is no controller and the state is no longer provisioning. The banner says "your messages are still queued here" and the backend comments promise a retry, but those messages can never be sent. The only option left is to kill the session.

Suggest adding a retry action for failed provisioning, or at least keeping Resume visible.

[P1] Remove the full Windows line separator when joining. In @xterm/xterm 5.5, SelectionService joins selected rows with `
` when `Browser.isWindows`. Splitting only on `
` leaves `` at the end of every segment, so joining `hello
world` produces `helloworld`. That puts a bare carriage return in the clipboard instead of a continuous line. Please handle CRLF as one boundary and add a Win32 regression test that covers both joined and preserved row breaks.

[P1] Preserve row boundaries for rectangular selections. xterm uses a separate COLUMN mode for Alt-drag on Windows and Linux, and its selection text intentionally contains one line per selected buffer row. `getSelectionPosition()` exposes only the start and end coordinates, so this helper cannot distinguish that mode. If the underlying first row fills the grid, this code flattens a rectangular selection such as `bc\nhi` into `bchi`. Track or read the selection mode and bypass the visual-wrap heuristic for column selections, with an Alt-drag regression test.

[P2] Inspect only the current visible columns. xterm documents that `IBufferLine.length` can exceed `Terminal.cols` because a line may retain cells after a resize. `translateToString(false)` reads that entire backing line, so the final character checked here may be outside the current grid. Stale tail content or padding can make a visibly short row join, or make a visibly full row keep its newline. Bound the translation to `term.cols` and add a resize-shaped test where the backing line is wider than the terminal.

FormRequest isn't keyed by `requestId`, so if a new question replaces the old one without unmounting, `useState` keeps the old values and the effect writes them under the new request's key. Suggest `key={requestId}`.
This scans all of localStorage and parses every draft on every keystroke. Could we prune once on mount or app start instead?

This writes a draft on mount even if nothing was edited, so every question shown leaves an entry. Questions the agent cancels are never cleared, so those entries stay for 7 days. Could we skip the write until the first edit?

`!installationKnown ? null` hides the Install/actions for any agent whose readiness is missing or `unknown`. `installationKnown` is false not only 'before the first observation' but also when the readiness query errors (`agents.error`) or the agent is absent from the response. Previously the install controls were driven by the installer plan and stayed usable; now a failed/erroring readiness fetch leaves every uninstalled row with no actions (only the error banner), and the silent refresh's failure is swallowed so nothing recovers it. Consider falling back to the installer plan when readiness has errored, or distinguishing 'loading' from 'unknown'.

For a not-yet-observed installation this shows `settings.harness.loginUnknown` (login-status wording) on a row that isn't installed; the summary is about installation, not login. Use an installation-specific unknown string.

The page-open refresh silently swallows both `error` and thrown failures, and `useEnsureAgentReadiness()` was removed from this component. If `/agents/refresh` fails, no readiness re-fetch or ensure happens at all, so stale/unknown state persists with no feedback. At minimum invalidate the readiness query (or fall back to ensure) on failure.

The restore command now passes `-t ""` but not `--interactive`. `GetLaunchCommand` in this same file pairs `-t ""` with `--interactive`, and the adapter's own comments say `-t <text>` mode exits once the prompt completes.

Without `--interactive`, a restored session will probably resume, run one empty turn (or reject the empty message), and exit. The terminal never reaches an input prompt, so any prompt AO sends afterwards has nowhere to go.

Suggested fix, matching the launch command:

```go
cmd = append(cmd, "-t", "", "--interactive", "--resume", "--session-id", agentSessionID)
```

The expected arguments in `goose_test.go` would need the same update. (I found this by reading the code; I haven't tested a restore against Goose 1.45+.)

**High: race can leave a session stuck in `provisioning`**

`UpdateSession` now writes back `provision_state` and `provision_error`. Lifecycle writes like `mutate` and `MarkSpawned` read the whole row, then write it back later, and nothing orders them with `SetSessionProvisionState`.

In `completeAsyncChatSpawn`, `DrainChatQueue` starts the first turn and `setProvisionState(ready)` runs right after. The first turn triggers lifecycle activity writes at that moment, so one of them can read `provisioning` and save it back after `ready` has landed.

Result: the UI shows "Starting…" permanently, `reconcileLive` skips the row, and on the next restart `FailInterruptedProvisioning` marks a working session as failed. The same race can also turn `failed` back into `provisioning`.

Suggested fix: leave the provision columns out of `UpdateSession` and change them only through `SetSessionProvisionState`.

**Medium: the discarded speculative session's branch is never deleted**

Closing the New Task dialog (or TTL expiry) removes the worktree and deletes the hidden row, but the branch `ao/<id>/root` stays behind. Session numbers come from `MAX(num)+1`, so the next dialog open or spawn gets the same ID again.

For single-repo projects, `Create` → `addWorktree` finds `refs/heads/<branch>` already exists and checks out that old branch. The new worker then starts from `main` as it was when the first dialog opened, which could be days old.

This used to take a rare failed spawn; now every open-and-close of the dialog triggers it. Workspace projects get a `-2` suffixed branch instead.

Suggested fix: delete the branch (when it has no commits beyond its base) as part of discarding the preparation.

**Medium: spawn attachments are lost if the start fails before this point**

The opening prompt names `.ao-attachments/attachment-N` right away, but the attachment files are only stored here, once the worktree exists. If the start fails earlier (worktree or provisioning error, or a daemon restart), the files are gone, and `retryFailedChatSpawn` builds its config without `Attachments`.

Result: "Retry start" launches the agent with instructions that point at files that don't exist, which breaks the banner's promise that the user's input is saved.

Suggested fix: store the attachment files before starting the async work (or keep them with the queued input) so retry can write them.

**Medium: retry-with-resume can fail the user's queued messages**

When the session already has a `ProviderConversationID`, this calls `resumeAgentRecordWithPolicy` while the row is still `failed`. `chat.Start` then sees `queuedAheadOfFirstController == false` and runs `settleOrphanedWork`, which marks every queued turn as failed.

Scenario: the daemon restarts after the controller is committed but before `ready`, or a start fails after that commit. On retry, the user's queued messages are marked failed, and the `DrainChatQueue` that follows has nothing to send.

Suggested fix: set the row back to `provisioning` before resuming, as the other retry path already does.

This constructs ActivitySignal directly instead of running the installed `ao hooks claude-code session-start` command and forwarding its request. Fixed in 7af7745d9: opening attachments are stored canonically before the prompt is queued and before the async response. Fixed in 7af7745d9: provider-conversation retry now enters provisioning before resume, so Chat preserves the queued turns; failures restore failed state. Tests cover successful queue draining and resume-error preservation.

**Data loss risk (blocking):** In workspace-project sessions, if a child repo (e.g. "api") is killed with saved edits (`PreservedRef=X`, state `active`) while the root stays clean, and the daemon later restarts with a *different* repo dirty, the restore-marker reconciliation can fall into the fallback branch that re-adds "api" via `ListWorkspaceRepos` with no knowledge of its `PreservedRef`. The subsequent `writeWorkspaceProjectRowState(ctx, row, "active", false)` call (keepPreserved=false) then upserts `PreservedRef=""` for that row, and since the upsert is `ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE SET preserved_ref = excluded.preserved_ref`, this silently overwrites and destroys the previously-preserved snapshot — with no error, before `ReapplyPreservedEdits` was ever called. This directly undermines the feature's core guarantee that saved edits stick around until the user asks for them back. Worth adding a regression test for: child-repo-only dirty kill, followed by a daemon restart triggered by a different repo's shutdown marker.

`archiveNotices` is an unbounded map keyed by session ID that's written on every interactive `Kill` and never pruned — it grows for the life of the daemon process. It also only exists to smuggle `Kill`'s outcome across a runtime type-assertion (`s.manager.(interface{ LastArchiveNotice(...) })`) in service.go, rather than returning the outcome directly from `Manager.Kill` the way the service layer already does with `KillOutcome`. Not urgent, but worth simplifying — either prune on read or widen the `Kill` signature instead of adding a second synchronized map.

Minor perf nit: `before, _ := w.gitCombined(ctx, statusPorcelainArgs(info.Path))` runs unconditionally before the cherry-pick attempt, but `before` is only read inside the `if applyErr != nil` branch below. On every successful `ApplyPreserved` call (the common case for both the reapply-edits endpoint and `RestoreAll`'s automatic replay), this spawns an extra `git status` subprocess whose result is discarded. Consider moving the `before` snapshot inside the error branch, or skip it entirely on the happy path.

`Restore` calls `w.refExists(ctx, repo, "refs/heads/"+recreateBranch)` here to enforce the new must-already-exist rule, then unconditionally calls `addWorktree`, which re-derives the identical `refExists` check internally (around line 1400) to decide its own branch-exists/create-new-branch fork. Every `Restore` that reaches this path now pays for two `git rev-parse --verify` calls for the same ref. Consider threading the already-known boolean through to `addWorktree` instead of recomputing it.

**Cancelled preparation leaks the worktree/branch.** Cleanup is keyed on `ws.Path != ""`, but `gitworktree.Create` returns a zero `WorkspaceInfo` on error and has no rollback. If the user opens New Task and closes it while `git worktree add` is running, the context cancel kills git after it may already have created the branch, the directory and the registration. `ws.Path` is empty, so nothing is destroyed; `cleanupTaskPreparation` then calls `deletePreparedBranches` with an empty `ws` (no-op) and deletes the row. The stale `ao/<id>/root` branch, partial directory and registration remain, and startup reclaim can't find them because the row never recorded a path. Since session IDs are `MAX(num)+1`, the next preparation can reuse the ID and hit `prepared workspace path %q already exists` (`workspace.go`, `FreshBranch` path). Suggest deriving the managed path/branch up front and cleaning them up on any error, not only when `ws.Path` was returned.

**No dedupe/cap on prepare.** `TaskComposer` POSTs this on every mount (including the CommandPalette embed and StrictMode double-mounts). Each call burns a session number, inserts a hidden row, runs a `git fetch` and a worktree add, and stays on disk for up to the 5-minute TTL. There's no per-project limit or reuse of an outstanding preparation, so repeated opens or a scripted client cause real git/disk churn. Consider reusing an in-flight preparation per project and/or capping outstanding ones.

**`queuedAheadOfFirstController` is keyed on `ProvisionState`, not on whether a controller ever ran.** A retry of a failed start is also `provisioning`, so `settleOrphanedWork` (and the provider-boundary logic below) is skipped for a genuinely dead controller. Scenario: async start dispatches the opening turn (`running`), the daemon restarts before mark-ready, `FailInterruptedProvisioning` marks it failed, user clicks Retry. The stale `running` turn is never settled: permanent spinner, and it can block queue draining. A transient `GetSession` error also returns `false` here, which would fail the user's queued opening prompt as orphaned. Suggest keying this on 'no prior controller/turns exist' rather than on provision state alone.

**Drain failure is logged, then the session is marked ready anyway.** If the controller dies between `launchChatController` and `DrainChatQueue`, this logs and falls through to `setProvisionState(Ready)`. Sends then get `ErrNoController`, the queued opening prompt sits in a session that reads as ready, and on a later resume `Start` runs `settleOrphanedWork` (state is no longer provisioning) and fails the brief with 'controller ended before the turn completed'. The brief is lost with no failed state or Retry banner. The retry path (lines 279/303) already treats a drain error as a failure; this path should too.

**Background half of async spawn runs outside the per-project workspace gate.** `acquireWorkspaceGate` serialises spawn/restore/cleanup per project, but async `Spawn` releases it right after `beginAsyncChatSpawn`, and `PrepareTaskWorkspace` never takes it. Quick successive task creations, or a prepare plus a spawn, now run `git fetch` and `git worktree add` concurrently in one repo, and concurrently with Restore/Cleanup of the same project. Git ref/worktree lock contention ('unable to lock') can then leave sessions in `failed` where they used to be serialised.

**No guard for `ProvisionState == provisioning`, and the resume guard is released early.** `retryFailedChatSpawn` hands the start to a background goroutine and returns, but `defer m.endAgentResume(id)` (line 2466) still runs on return. A second `ResumeAgentWithMode` (double click, CLI/API; the UI hides the button but other callers exist) reads a `provisioning` row, skips this `failed` branch and takes the ordinary resume path, starting a second controller while the background start launches one. `asyncChatSpawns[id]` is also overwritten. Suggest rejecting/joining when the session is already provisioning, or holding the resume guard until the background start finishes.

**Boot-blocking housekeeping.** `FailInterruptedProvisioning` joins per-session errors from `setProvisionState` (an UPDATE plus a read), and any error here is returned from `ReconcileStartupSafety`, which makes `daemon.go` abort with 'reconcile sessions on boot'. One locked/failing row would stop the daemon from starting over a state flag. The same applies to `CleanupInterruptedTaskPreparations` just above (line 3174), which additionally does git worktree teardown and branch deletion synchronously before the API listener binds, so a slow or unreachable repo delays startup. Suggest logging these errors and moving the git work to `ReconcileBackground`.

**Loosened invariant on the general restore path.** `AddExclude` failure used to abort `restoreAttachments`; it's now a warning, and this applies to every restore, not just the async one. The exclude keeps the attachments dir out of `git status`; if it fails (read-only `info/exclude`, lock) the agent's `git add -A` can commit the user's attached files to the branch/PR. It also changes behavior unrelated to async spawn (AGENTS.md: keep changes surgical). If best-effort is only wanted for the async path, please make it local to that caller.

**Multi-repo create drops the pre-resolved `seedRef` guarantee.** `CreateWorkspaceProject` used to resolve `seedRef`/`baseRef` for every repo before creating the first worktree, so a later repo couldn't fail after earlier worktrees existed. Delegating to `addWorktree` re-lists worktree records per repo and re-derives the seed as `origin/<branch>` from `baseRef`; its existing-local-branch path attaches a leftover branch without a base resolve. A multi-repo workspace can be seeded from a different commit than the pre-resolved `seedRef`, and for recovered repos `BaseSHA` is the current base-ref tip rather than the original, so `DeletePreparedBranch` never matches and the branch leaks. (The error message still reports `seedRef`, which is no longer what was used.)

**Approval switches that launch identically are rejected.** `ApprovalFixedAtLaunch(..., nil)` gives the validator no launch value. `cline --acp` only gets `--auto-approve true` for auto and bypass-permissions; default and accept-edits launch identically, and accept-edits is resolved per request by `StandardPermissionPolicy()`. `applyTurnSettings` runs the validator every turn with the launch-time mode, so a Chat started in default that switches to accept-edits, or one started in auto that switches to bypass, fails with `ErrACPSetterUnsupported` ('restart Chat'). Passing a `launchValue` that maps default/accept-edits to `""` and auto/bypass to `"auto"` would allow both, as Goose already does with `gooseMode`.

**`PrepareACPAgent` clobbers the shared `.kiro/agents/ao.json`.** It calls `writeKiroHooks(..., systemPrompt, "", ports.AgentConfig{})`, so `setKiroAgentDefaults` runs `delete(topLevel, "model")` (empty `AgentConfig.Model`) and replaces the `file://` prompt written by `GetAgentHooks` with the inline `systemPrompt` (or null when empty). If a Chat launch and a TUI launch share a worktree, e.g. after an interface handoff, the Chat launch silently drops the TUI agent's configured model and prompt-file reference. The inline prompt is also written into the checkout rather than the session-private prompt directory.

**`config["permission"]` is replaced wholesale.** `existing` comes from `cfg.Env["KILO_CONFIG_CONTENT"]`; if it already carries a permission map such as `{"webfetch":"deny","bash":"ask"}`, any non-default AO mode overwrites it with `{"edit":"allow"}` or `{"*":"allow"}`, and the user's deny/ask rules are lost. The `agent` map is merged correctly; the `permission` map should be merged the same way (AO's entries layered over the inherited ones, without loosening rules AO doesn't own).

**PATH fallback is unreachable when the CLI isn't found.** `resolveAdapterBinary` returns early when `plugin.ResolveBinary` fails, so a user with `autohand-acp` on PATH or in an npm global directory, but whose `autohand` CLI the plugin can't find, gets 'autohand-acp is not installed' even though the adapter exists. The comment promises a PATH/common-locations fallback, but it only runs once the CLI has resolved and no sibling is found. The adapter lookup should not depend on the CLI resolving. `vibeacp`'s resolver has the same shape.

**`SiblingBinary` is too permissive.** It only checks `!info.IsDir()` and never the Unix executable bit, and `filepath.Dir(reference)` on a bare or empty reference gives `"."`, so the stat runs against the daemon's working directory. A stray non-executable `vibe-acp` or `autohand-acp` beside the reference is returned and then fails at exec time instead of falling back to `ResolveBinary`. Suggest returning `""` for a bare/relative reference and checking the exec bit on non-Windows.

**Duplicated with `autohandacp`.** Both packages define the same plugin subset interface, an `acpAdapter struct{ plugin }` overriding `ResolveBinary`, and a resolver calling `SiblingBinary` then `binaryutil.ResolveBinary`. Any fix, such as the fallback issue noted on `autohandacp/driver.go`, has to be made twice. A shared helper in `nativeacp` or `binaryutil` (e.g. `nativeacp.SiblingPlugin(plugin, spec)`) would remove the duplication.

**Regression: human/automation/daemon messages lose literal-text guarantee when they contain a session link** When `body` (or `preview`) contains an `ao://sessions/...` link, this now routes the *entire* message through `ChatMarkdown` (full GFM) instead of the plain `

`. `ChatMarkdown`'s `p` renderer has no `whitespace-pre-wrap`, so: - Manual line breaks in a multi-line human message collapse (GFM treats a single `\n` as a soft break, rendered as normal HTML whitespace with no `pre-wrap`). - Any GFM-significant characters in the raw text (`#`, `*`, `-`, backticks, `>`, etc.) now get reinterpreted as headings/lists/emphasis/code/blockquotes instead of rendering literally. Concrete repro: a user pastes a multi-line message such as `"Notes:\n- fix bug\nao://sessions/proj/sess\n- write test"`. Before this PR it rendered as literal text with the newlines preserved; after, it renders as a bulleted list with the newlines lost, because the mere presence of the session link switches the whole message to markdown rendering. Same issue applies to the `OriginMessage` `preview` branch a few lines below (~line 664).

This component plus the new `ui-store` fields (`sessionLinkError`, `sessionLinkNotices`, `sessionLinkNoticeSequence`, `showSessionLinkNotice`, `dismissSessionLinkNotice`) reimplement a stacked, auto-dismissing, top-center notification overlay that already exists as `GlobalToast` / `useUiStore().showGlobalToast` (see `frontend/src/renderer/components/GlobalToast.tsx` and `globalToasts`/`showGlobalToast`/`dismissGlobalToast` in `ui-store.ts`). `GlobalToast` already supports a stack, `top-center` placement, per-item dismiss timers, and an `error` tone.

The only capability missing there is a manual per-item dismiss button. Extending `GlobalToast`/`GlobalToastItem` with an optional dismiss button (and reusing `showGlobalToast(message, undefined, "top-center")` for termination notices, "error" tone for the malformed/missing-session banner) would avoid a second parallel state shape, component, and set of CSS classes to maintain for the same visual pattern.

**Queued with nothing running isn't only a held queue.** This state also happens on every normal send: `sendLocked` saves the turn as `queued`, and `dispatch` only moves it to `running` after `SendTurn` returns and `BindTurnToProvider` runs. If the renderer reads a snapshot in that gap:

- The Working bar here disappears, so the message just sits in the queued dock with no sign the agent is working.
- `willQueue` (line ~1433) is false, so the composer says "Enter to send" and "Message the agent…". A second message typed in that gap actually gets queued: `Send` waits for the dispatch lock, then sees the agent busy. That's the same label mismatch this PR is trying to fix.

The old `Boolean(turn)` check handled this gap. Suggestion: only treat the queue as held when the most recent finished turn is `failed` or `recovered`, or have the daemon send an explicit held flag in the snapshot.

**[medium] Stale active turn survives into a new conversation**

The active-turn file and event journal are keyed by AO session (`AOSessionID`), not by provider conversation. Neither is reset when a new conversation starts, and the stale turn is only cleared here if the journal already shows it completed.

Scenario: stop the session, switch agents, or crash the host mid-turn. `Terminate` kills the provider and the turn stays in `active/<session>.json`. On the next start or resume, the new provider loads it, and every `SendTurn` fails with "already has an active turn". The daemon's `Interrupt(<its turn id>)` is rejected too ("active turn is X, not Y"), so the user can't clear it. Un-acked journal frames from the old conversation are also replayed into the new one.

Suggest scoping the active turn and journal to the provider conversation id, or resetting them on a fresh start.

**[medium] Protocol version mismatch hangs instead of failing**

On a version mismatch, `pump` calls `c.fail` and returns without sending on `c.ready` and without emitting `ChatControllerStopped`. After an AO update that changes `protocolVersion`, a fresh `connect` blocks in `waitReady` until the caller's context expires instead of failing immediately. A live conversation just closes its events channel with no stopped state or error.

Suggest signalling `ready` with the error (or closing it so `waitReady` returns) and emitting a stopped event with the reason.

**[medium] Replay failure leaks the freshly started host**

If `replay` fails here (5s timeout), only `conv.Close()` runs. The host just started keeps running, and the fresh provider id is discarded. Every later `Start` for this session reconnects to the orphaned host and returns `ErrChatRecoveryInconclusive` ("fresh Unreal Agent start found a live provider"), so the session is stuck until the host is killed by hand.

The `waitReady` failure path above calls `Terminate`. This path should do the same.

**[low] `interrupt()` can swallow a coordinator failure**

`interrupt()` receives from `runtime.done`, the same channel the main loop watches for coordinator failure. If the coordinator fails (e.g. an LLM error) while an interrupt is pending, `select` may pick the interrupt first. That call then consumes the failure, returns it as the interrupt's error, and leaves the active turn set with a dead coordinator. The provider keeps running with nothing processing its inbox, later turns are rejected or hang, and the failure never reaches the daemon.

Suggest a separate signal for interrupt completion, or re-broadcasting the failure (e.g. closing a channel and storing the error) so both readers see it.

**[low] `unreal-agent` is advertised in `--harness` but doesn't work from the CLI**

Nothing on the backend forces this chat-only harness into chat mode or sets bypass permissions. `ao spawn --harness unreal-agent` (or an orchestrator delegation without `mode`) takes the daemon default (TUI), and `GetLaunchCommand` then fails with "chat mode only". An explicit `--mode chat` still fails `validateStart`, because the CLI has no way to pass an approval mode. Only the desktop TaskComposer works around this.

Suggest defaulting chat-only harnesses to chat mode (and the required approval mode) server-side, or dropping it from the help text until the CLI supports it.

**[low] Auth probe ignores project env**

`AuthStatus` reads the provider and API key only from the daemon's own environment (`os.Getenv`). The model catalog reads the per-project env map, and the provider process is launched with that project env merged in. If the key (e.g. `OPENAI_API_KEY`) is set only in project env, `Probe` returns `ErrChatAuthRequired` and chat never starts, even though the provider would authenticate. It can also report the wrong provider when `UNREAL_HARNESS_LLM_PROVIDER` is set per project.

**[low] Cumulative usage resets after provider restart**

Usage is accumulated in the in-memory `runtime.usage`, but `ChatUsage` totals are meant to be cumulative for the conversation. After the provider process restarts (host death, then resume), the count starts from 0, so the token totals shown for the conversation go backwards.

Suggest persisting the running totals alongside the journal, or restoring them from it on resume.

**An old draft can be restored into a different question that reuses the request id.**

A draft is only cleared after this dock resolves the question successfully (`resolve` → `clearElicitationDraft`), and it is keyed by `(sessionId, requestId)`. Request ids are not always unique within a session. The legacy ACP transport numbers them `ao-legacy-%d` from a per-transport counter (`backend/internal/adapters/chatdriver/acp/legacy.go:149`), and that counter starts over when the agent process restarts.

Scenario: the user half-types an answer to `ao-legacy-1`. Then the question goes away without this dock submitting it: the agent cancels it, another window answers it, or the session restarts. The draft stays in storage for up to 7 days. The next `ao-legacy-1` question in that session restores it here:
- `restoreValues` fills in any field whose name matches (e.g. `answer`), so an answer to an unrelated question shows up pre-filled and can be submitted.
- `activeQuestion` is restored without clamping. If it is `>= questionGroups.length`, `visibleProperties` falls back to showing every property and the step-by-step flow breaks.

Possible fixes:
- Clear the draft whenever the request resolves or disappears from the snapshot, not only after a successful local submit.
- Save a fingerprint of the schema or question text with the draft and ignore the draft on read if it doesn't match.
- Clamp the restored `activeQuestion` to `questionGroups.length - 1`.

[P1] Serialize attachment replay with direct staging. The row publishes `workspace_path` here before `restoreAttachments`, so a concurrent `StageAttachments` reads the non-empty path and calls `attachments.Put`. `Put` creates the canonical file and then writes the worktree with no-replace semantics, while `MaterializeWorkspace` can see that same canonical entry and write the same destination with `replace=true`. If replay wins, `Put` gets `ErrExists`, removes the canonical copy as rollback, and the user attachment send fails, leaving only an orphaned worktree file. The current publication test blocks before this update, so it does not exercise the post-publish/pre-replay window. Please serialize these operations per session or make the concurrent projection idempotent without deleting the canonical copy.

[P2] Keep ownership of a cancelled claimed preparation until it finishes cleanup. On context cancellation this cancels creation, marks the visible session failed, and returns without waiting for `prep.done`. The claim already removed this preparation from `taskPreparations` and stopped its timer. If creation then returns a partial worktree, `SetSessionProvisionedWorkspace` is rejected because the row is no longer `provisioning`; if `Destroy` refuses that partial worktree as dirty, its path survives only on the abandoned preparation object. The visible row has no `workspace_path`, restart cleanup skips it because it was promoted, and nothing can reclaim the worktree or branch. I reproduced this with a blocking `Create` that returns a partial path after cancellation and a dirty-worktree `Destroy`. Please wait for/transfer cleanup ownership, or durably record the partial workspace before abandoning the preparation.

[P1] Keep the session non-retryable until this claimed preparation has relinquished cleanup ownership. When the preparation finishes, the old worker calls `cleanupAsyncChatWorkspace` outside the project workspace gate and can race the retry that is reusing/provisioning the same worktree—publishing stale metadata or removing the retry workspace after a transient first cleanup failure. I reproduced the overlap by blocking preparation creation, cancelling it, invoking Resume after the failed-state write, and then releasing creation. Please defer the failed/retryable state until cleanup completes, or reject Resume while the prior async spawn is still present (and avoid replacing its run entry).

`value <= now` allows no skew, and a failed check deletes the entry, both in `readElicitationDraft` (78-84) and in the sweep. `Date.now()` is wall-clock time, so if the clock steps back after an edit (manual fix, VM or dual-boot RTC correction, a big NTP step), a just-written draft looks future-dated and gets wiped. That's rare, but it's the exact loss this PR is preventing. A small skew allowance (e.g. `value - now <= SKEW_MS && now - value <= MAX_AGE_MS`) still rejects corrupt far-future values. **P1 — inventory overlay can clobber a concurrent fail notify**

Reconcile first copies post-`reloadRevision` notifications into `fresh`, then unconditionally assigns inventory rows:

```go
fresh[server.Name] = domain.ConversationMCPServer{
    Name:   server.Name,
    Status: server.Status, // always ready from the adapter
    ...
}
```

The adapter marks every `ServerInfo` row as ready. `applyMCPServers` can record a *failed* startup notify after the status-list returns and before this block takes `mcpPersistMu` (event pump is concurrent; the mutex only serializes the durable write). That failure is then overwritten to ready with empty error fields — banner clears while tools are still missing.

When merging `result.Servers` into `fresh`, do not overwrite an entry that is already present from `seenRevision > reloadRevision` with a non-ready status (prefer the newer startup notification over the list snapshot).

**Regression test**

[P2] Preserve case-insensitive project overrides on Windows

`termtheme.Apply` checks only exact uppercase keys. On Windows, a project env entry such as `term_theme=dark` is equivalent to `TERM_THEME`, but this call adds a second uppercase value from the theme file. Both keys then reach ConPTY; map iteration makes their order unstable, and Windows environment deduplication keeps whichever case variant appears last. The explicit project value can therefore be lost nondeterministically. Please make this lookup/normalization case-insensitive when `envKeysCaseInsensitive` is true and add a Windows-semantics test.

A blank variant is removed, so the value written in its place is the only one left.

Was that a deliberate simplicity-over-throughput tradeoff, or worth narrowing to a per-run (or per-PR) lock before concurrent reviewer load becomes a bottleneck? A per-run key (e.g. a map of mutexes keyed by `run.ID`, cleaned up after) would keep the same duplicate-publish protection without serializing unrelated PRs' network calls behind each other.

**Test connection now spends 2 auth failures per tap.**

`reloadConfig()` goes `resolveActiveConfig` → `connectHost` → `deps.refreshEndpoints(config)`, which is `fetchAdvertisedEndpoints(baseUrl, config.password)` (`lib/connectRuntime.ts:120-124`) — an **authenticated** request whose failure is swallowed by `connectHost`'s catch (`lib/connect.ts:80`). With a rotated password that 401s, and then `pingServer` 401s again.

Two failed attempts per tap, so 3 taps arm the daemon's lockout. `lib/api.ts:410-421` documents exactly this constraint ("locks a device out for a minute after 5 failed auths") and `getSessions` was deliberately restructured to cap a bad-credential tick at a single attempt. The `if (!answered)` guard below exists to avoid spending that second attempt — but an extra one is reintroduced here, ahead of the ping, where the guard can't help.

**`errorStatus === null` renders as a red error before the first poll.**

Store initial state is `connection: "closed"` (`store.tsx:148`) and `errorStatus: null` (`store.tsx:152`). Once `configured` flips true but before the first poll sets `"connecting"`, `describeDesktopStatus` falls through to the `default` branch → red **"Offline"** — or red **"Address changed"** when `activeEndpoints` is tunnel-only, since `tunnelMayHaveRotated(..., connection === "open")` is also true in that window.

The board runs the identical computation but only renders it behind `error ?` (`app/(tabs)/index.tsx:176`); that gate wasn't carried over here. `null` needs to distinguish "no poll has failed *yet*" from "unreachable".

**Unguarded `await reloadConfig()` — a rejection here leaves the screen stuck.**

`reloadConfig` is `try { … } finally { setConfigResolved(true) }` with no `catch` (`store.tsx:228-259`). Two unprotected rejection paths: `resolveActiveConfig`'s fallback `loadLegacyConfig()` sits outside its own try (`lib/resolveConfig.ts:53`), and `await activeHost()` at `store.tsx:255` is outside everything. Both are storage/keychain reads — a failure mode `hosts.ts` explicitly designs around.

`onForget` has no catch around this, so on rejection the user gets no alert and no navigation to onboarding, just a stopped spinner — the same stale-screen outcome this handler was written to prevent.

Related: `reloadConfig`'s doc comment still claims "Always resolves to something: every failure path inside falls back to the last stored config", which is no longer true of the `activeHost()` line.

Non-blocking: on a 5xx, `answered` is true so `refresh()` is skipped — the test row reads "Desktop error" while the status row directly above can still read "Connected" until the next poll tick. The comment justifies the skip by lockout cost, which applies to 401/429 but not to a 5xx.

The last two /proc/stat CPU fields, guest and guest_nice, are already included in user and nice on Linux. This loop adds them again to both busy and total, so the host CPU percentage is overstated when a VM consumes CPU. For example, 100 user ticks (including 100 guest) plus 100 idle ticks is 50% busy, but this calculation reports about 67%. Please exclude fields 8 and 9 from the aggregate and add a fixture with nonzero guest time.

live sessions at risk; worst case, a session keeps working on the old

**Fallback covers the symptom you'd actually hit in the wild.** The

The user sees Q2 with no indication that Q1 failed or needs retrying. **[P1] Reconcile failed drafts and boundaries for requests outside partial pages**

When `hasMoreBefore` is true, this passes `fullyLoaded=false`, so a request id that is no longer in `snapshot.items` is deliberately retained. If a failed-save question is answered remotely or times out after it falls outside the loaded 200-row window, its localStorage draft and `elicitation-persistence-failed` boundary are never cleared. The sweep is only triggered opportunistically by this effect, not on a timer, so the stale answer can remain indefinitely and keep blocking navigation or quit. Please obtain all pending request ids from the daemon, or track completion separately, and clear both the draft and per-request boundary once the request is no longer pending.

**[P2] Drop failed-draft memory entries during external resolution**

`unsavedElicitationDrafts` stores the entire answer after a failed localStorage write, but the reconciliation path only removes the storage key; it never calls `forgetUnsavedElicitationDraft`. If another window or mobile answers the request, or it times out, the answer remains in this module-level map until renderer exit and could win over storage if the same key is ever mounted again. Please expose per-request cleanup and invoke it from reconciliation or expiry, not only from this dock local success path.

**Bug: `IsAlive` returning `(false, nil)` after a failed `Destroy` is not proof the runtime is gone.**

conpty's `IsAlive` (`adapters/runtime/conpty/runtime.go:357`) doesn't check the process. It dials the host's loopback listener and treats a refused connection as definitively gone. But conpty's `Destroy` first sends the graceful shutdown (`killHost`), which closes that listener, and only then waits for the PID to exit.

Scenario (Windows): the pty-host stops listening but hangs during shutdown, and `process.Kill()` fails (e.g. access denied). `Destroy` returns `pty-host pid N is still alive after teardown` (`runtime.go:298`). This re-probe then gets a refused connection and returns `(false, nil)`, so `Kill` marks the row terminated and removes the worktree while the pty-host and its agent child keep running with no row pointing at them. That's the exact "possibly-live agent with no owner" outcome the doc comment above says to avoid. Before this change, `Kill` returned the error and could be retried.

Suggest dropping the runtime tolerance here and failing closed on any `Destroy` error, as before this PR. Every runtime's `Destroy` already returns `nil` when it confirms absence (tmux via `confirmedAbsentOutput`, conpty when the registry has no entry), so any error it does return means the runtime may still be alive. Re-probing can only turn a safe failure into an unsafe success. The workspace and teardown-budget fixes in this PR still cover the #5463 stranding.

If tolerance is still wanted, it needs process-level evidence, e.g. `ProbeFencedRuntime` and continuing only on `FencedDead`, not the listener-based `IsAlive`.

[P1] Prevent reviewer hooks from updating the worker session

A Claude worker already installs lifecycle hooks in `<workspace>/.claude/settings.local.json`. Returning here only skips installation; the reviewer still loads that file and inherits the worker credentials. In a local probe, the reviewer SessionStart hook replaced the worker native session ID through `SetWorkerActivity`. Reviewer SessionEnd then marked the live worker `exited`, so `IssueTerminalTicket` rejected it with `terminal session exited`. `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` does not isolate [project-local settings](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings). Suppress or separately route reviewer lifecycle hooks while preserving the worker hooks, and add a regression for a worker and reviewer sharing one workspace.

[P2] Preserve compatibility with pre-upgrade idempotency receipts

Existing `project.create` receipts store the original input, but normalization now runs before building the payload used by `loadIdempotentProject`. Retrying an unchanged request and key with legacy `config: {"workerAgent":"codex"}` compares the stored alias against the new nested role and returns `ErrIdempotencyMismatch`, or HTTP 409. The same receipt accepted its retry on main and rejected it on this head in a PostgreSQL probe. The GitHub create paths have the same ordering. Preserve the receipt payload while normalizing the persisted config, or compare old and new receipts consistently, and add an upgrade retry regression.

**Medium — Map string offsets to terminal cells before constructing the link range.** `match.start` and `endOffset` are JavaScript string offsets, but xterm ranges use terminal cell coordinates. For example, in `中 ao://sessions/p/s`, the URL starts at column 4 because `中` occupies two cells, while this calculation reports column 3. Combining characters cause the opposite mismatch, and wrapped links can also be assigned to the wrong row, leaving visible portions unclickable or making adjacent text activate the link. Please translate offsets through the buffer cells and their widths, as xterm's own link provider does: https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/blob/master/addons/addon-web-links/src/WebLinkProvider.ts. Add tests asserting the actual start/end ranges for wide and combining characters before a URL, including a wrapped case; the current terminal tests assert text and activation but not coordinates.

Fixed in 94c95836c. `repoMayHoldConfig` no longer uses a fixed ref list. It checks the tip of `HEAD` and every ref a session could be attached to or seeded from: all local branches (`refs/heads`), remote-tracking branches (`refs/remotes`) and tags (`refs/tags`). `TestConfiguredDefaultUnresolvedWhenAnySeedRefHoldsConfig` reproduces your case: HEAD and the checkout have no `.github/copilot/settings.json`, the config is committed only on a local branch, and a real `git worktree add` of that branch contains it. **Blocking — `AO_DATA_DIR` is ignored.** This always resolves under `~/.ao`, so `AO_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ao-lab-data` (the documented lab isolation, and what `test/e2e-pod/real-app.spec.ts` sets) still writes to — and can rotate — the real installation's log. `resolvedDaemonDataDir()` already encodes the override; derive the log from it and keep the current default when no override is set. The keep-daemon path at line 1646 has the identical bug and should be fixed in the same change, otherwise the two writers still disagree under an override.

**Medium — the exit marker is not a terminator.** The stamp is written on `exit`, but stdio can still hold buffered output at that point (the comment two lines above says exactly this). Demonstrated: with the parent not draining, `exit` fires before 60 KB of stderr is delivered.

```
[['exit',0],['data',60000],['close',null]]
```

So the log ends with the panic stack and the `[ao] daemon exited with SIGSEGV` line sits mid-file — the opposite of the stated goal. Write the stamp in the `close` handler, immediately before `closeDaemonLog()`, so it lands after the drained output. That is also what the 23 Sep review asked for, along with a test that delivers stderr after `exit` and asserts it precedes the marker; that test is still missing.

**Medium — this assertion is timing-dependent and fails most runs here.** 4 of 5 local runs fail with `ENOENT ... daemon.log.1`.

Cause: the first `writeDaemonLog` crosses the threshold and calls `openDaemonLog`, which calls `closeDaemonLog()` without awaiting the replaced stream's flush. The test's `await closeDaemonLog()` only awaits the *new* stream, so the 40 bytes may still be unflushed when the second `openDaemonLog` runs `statSync` — it reads 0, skips the rename, and `.1` never appears.

This also means `openDaemonLog` decides rotation from an on-disk size that can lag what was written, and resets `daemonLogBytes` to that stale value. Production self-corrects on the next chunk, but the counter under-counts and rotation can lag by a chunk. Prefer tracking bytes in memory (or awaiting the previous stream's `end` before re-statting) so the decision is deterministic.
Nit — a test-only export in a shipped module. The late-error case can be covered by holding the stream through a rotation triggered by `writeDaemonLog`, without widening the production surface.

Nit — "this same file" is not true in dev: keep-daemon writes `~/.ao/daemon.log` (main.ts:1646) while this writer uses `~/.ao/dev/daemon.log`. Worth fixing the comment, or better, having both paths share one resolver.

**Reviewers launched before this change will look dead after upgrade.** Reviews already persisted with a `LaunchID` were started without the `agent-process supervise` wrapper, so the exact supervised-process check won't find them. After an upgrade, the next list call (mobile polls every 2s) marks the in-flight review failed/exited. When the still-running reviewer later submits its result, that submission is rejected and lost, and triggering a new review destroys the live pane and launches a duplicate. Could this fall back to `IsChildAlive` when no supervised-process record exists for the launch, or only take this path for launches created by the supervise wrapper?

**A missing tmux session now errors instead of returning not-alive.** `IsChildAlive` reported `false, nil` when the session was gone. This path returns an error. If the reviewer's tmux session is killed outside AO: "Start review" fails every time instead of relaunching, restore never succeeds, and the list path treats the error as alive, so the review stays `running` forever. Suggest mapping a session-not-found result to `(false, nil)` here, the way the old check did.

**Exit reports from the supervisor go to the wrong endpoint.** `--session handleID` makes the supervisor post its exit report to `/sessions/<reviewer-handle>/activity`, but the reviewer handle isn't a session. Reviewer activity lives on `/reviews/{id}/activity`. Every exit gets a 404, which prints an error line into the reviewer pane and the hooks log, and the exited state is never recorded; it only gets corrected when some client lists reviews. The supervisor probably needs a review-scoped mode, or the exit report needs to be routed to the review activity endpoint.

**The `sessionId || reviewId` fallback contradicts the comment just above it.** If this screen opens without `sessionId` (e.g. from a deep link or notification route that only carries the review id), attachments get staged under `/sessions/<reviewId>/attachments`, which fails, so replies with attachments can't be sent. SSE refresh also subscribes to the wrong id, so live updates never arrive. Consider resolving the worker id from the review when `sessionId` is missing, or disabling attachments/SSE until it's known, rather than falling back to the review id.

**On tmux, every newly launched supervised reviewer is reported dead.** Reviewers now launch with `agent-process supervise --review <reviewID> --launch ...` (line 555), and `HasSupervisedProcessRecord` sees that supervisor through `isAnySupervisorCommand`, so this exact probe runs. But the tmux exact probe goes through `containsExactSupervisedWorkload`, which calls `isSupervisorCommand(cmd, sessionID, launchID)`, and that matcher only accepts `--session <sessionID>`. Here `ref.SessionID` is the handle (`review-<worker>`), and the process has `--review <reviewID>`, so it can never match.

Result: `Alive` returns false for a reviewer that is actually running, so it hits the same failure as before: the list call marks it failed/exited, its result submission is rejected, and re-triggering destroys the live pane. conpty isn't affected because it compares only `launchID`.

The launcher tests use `fakeRuntime`, and `TestHasSupervisedProcessRecordFindsAOReviewerSupervisor` covers only the record check, not the exact probe with a `--review` command, so CI stays green. Options: teach `isSupervisorCommand` to accept `--review <id>` and pass the review id in `ref`, or keep `--session <handle>` on the supervise argv and add a separate flag for the exit-report target.

**Once a supervised reviewer exits, this fallback reports it as alive.** When the reviewer's child exits, `agent-process supervise` exits too, and the pane drops to the preserved interactive shell (`exec "${SHELL:-/bin/sh}" -i`). `HasSupervisedProcessRecord` then returns `false`, because no supervisor is left in the tree. So this branch runs, and `IsChildAlive` returns `true` because the pane's shell is alive.

Reproduced on real tmux at 1791093 by launching with the launcher's argv, then killing the reviewer child:

```
reviewer running: IsChildAlive=true HasSupervisedProcessRecord=true  IsExact=true  launcher.Alive=(true,<nil>)
reviewer exited:  IsChildAlive=true HasSupervisedProcessRecord=false IsExact=false launcher.Alive=(true,<nil>)
```

That means the exact probe only runs while the reviewer is alive and is skipped once it has exited. In `review.go`:
- **Trigger (~417):** for a reviewer with an `AgentSessionID`, `Alive=true` reuses the handle and sends the new review task into the pane, which is now a bare shell. The run never starts and stays `running`.
- **Restore (~700, ~754):** returns "already alive" instead of relaunching.
- **List reconcile (~1116):** never marks the run failed/exited. The supervisor's exit report to `/reviews/{id}/activity` is then the only signal, and if that report is lost (e.g. the daemon is down when the reviewer exits) the review stays `running` indefinitely.

The fallback can't tell a legacy reviewer apart from a supervised reviewer that has exited, because both have no supervisor in the tree. `ReviewerLaunchID` alone doesn't help either: the earlier pre-supervisor launches also stored one. Some options:
- Persist on the review row whether the launch was supervised, and use the exact probe unconditionally when it was.
- Or, for the legacy path, require a non-shell child process in the pane (similar to what `containsManagedWorkload` does for the manual-relaunch case) instead of just a live pane.

A regression test would help here too. The current launcher tests use `fakeRuntime` with a static `supervisedRecord`, so they can't express "record disappears when the reviewer exits".

**Build break:** adding `IsUnsupervisedReviewerAlive` to `reviewerRuntime` means `runtimeselect.Runtime` no longer satisfies it:

```
internal/daemon/lifecycle_wiring.go:340:47: cannot use runtime (variable of interface type runtimeselect.Runtime) as reviewerRuntime value in argument to reviewcore.NewLauncher: runtimeselect.Runtime does not implement reviewerRuntime (missing method IsUnsupervisedReviewerAlive)
```

`hybridRuntime` implements the method, but the `runtimeselect.Runtime` interface (runtimeselect.go:20) doesn't declare it. Declaring it there, or adding a `ports` interface like `SupervisedProcessRecordInspector`, fixes the build. When I did that locally, two test fakes also need the method:
- `fakeBackend` / `restartableFakeBackend` in `runtimeselect/hybrid_test.go`, because the method has to go into `routedBackend` too. With the method on the interface, the type-assert fallback in `hybridRuntime.IsUnsupervisedReviewerAlive` can then become a direct call.
- `selectableRuntime` in `daemon/wiring_test.go`.

The launcher tests use `fakeRuntime`, which is why the review package tests pass while the daemon doesn't compile.

**On the default macOS/Linux runtime, a running reviewer is reported dead.** `hybridRuntime.Create` returns and stores `ptyhost-v1:review-mer-1`, so `Alive` gets the prefixed handle and puts it into `ref.SessionID`. `hybridRuntime.IsExactSupervisedProcessAlive` strips the prefix from the handle but passes `ref` through unchanged, and conpty's `IsSupervisedProcessAlive` then returns false because `string(ref.SessionID) != handle.ID` (`ptyhost-v1:review-mer-1` vs `review-mer-1`). The launcher sets `AO_RUNTIME_LAUNCH_ID`, so conpty has a launch record and `HasSupervisedProcessRecord` is true, which means the exact probe is always the one that runs.

Reproduced with `runtimeselect.New` on macOS, the launcher's supervise argv, and `AO_RUNTIME_LAUNCH_ID` set as `runtimeEnv` does:

```
runtime=*runtimeselect.hybridRuntime stored handle="ptyhost-v1:review-mer-1"
reviewer running:
  IsChildAlive=true HasSupervisedProcessRecord=true
  exact[ref.SessionID="ptyhost-v1:review-mer-1"]=false   <- what Alive passes
  exact[ref.SessionID="review-mer-1"]=true
  launcher.Alive=false
reviewer exited:
  IsChildAlive=false ... launcher.Alive=false
```

So a running reviewer gets the original failure: the list call marks the run failed/exited, the result submission is rejected, and triggering again replaces the live host. tmux isn't affected, because its handles aren't prefixed; that's why the earlier tmux repros passed.

One possible fix is in `hybridRuntime` (`IsExactSupervisedProcessAlive` / `IsSupervisedProcessAlive`): when `ref.SessionID` equals the prefixed `handle.ID`, rewrite it to `raw.ID` so the ref matches the routed handle. Another is to have the launcher build the ref from the logical reviewer id (`reviewerHandleID(workerID)`), the same id it passes to `supervise --session`, instead of the stored runtime handle. A hybrid-level test with a direct-prefixed handle would catch this; the current launcher tests use `fakeRuntime`, which ignores the ref's session id.

“Select model” removes the old error-like text, but the unresolved state still does not explain the implicit choice. Non-blocking edge: the title filter only enters title mode after at least one command digit here (`b >= '0'`), so an **empty-`Ps`** title — `ESC ] ; ✳ title BEL` or C1 `0x9D ; …` — passes through unchanged.

The downstream parser treats an empty `Ps` as command `0`, so the title still leaks. I reproduced it against the real `vt-go` emulator at this head: `ESC ] ; ✳ session title BEL` renders `session title` inside the composer and `LastBorderedPromptComposerState` returns `Draft`.

This is not the Claude shape from #5301 (`ESC ] 0 ;`), so it does not block the fix — flagging only because the filter is compensating for the parser and should agree with it. If you want to close it, treat an empty `Ps` as command `0` for both introducers.

P1 (blocking): this guard excludes every delta that carries a native `ProviderEventID`, which is exactly the persistent Claude/ACP path from #4657. `acp/client.go:570` copies the stable host event id into `ProviderEventID`, and `persistenthost/acp_relay.go` assigns one per `session/update`, so each Claude text chunk still reaches `ProjectProviderEvent` as its own archive/projection/CDC transaction. The SSE overlay hides the latency but SQLite stays globally blocked. Please preserve the individual dedupe/ack identities while committing adjacent identified deltas in one transaction, and add a persistent-host regression that asserts the reduced write count (the current `TestStreamingReplyCoalescesDeltaPersistence` only exercises anonymous deltas).

P2 (blocking): when a `message.completed` event carries no replacement text, `event.text ?? ""` replaces the accumulated live answer with an empty string. `ChatEvent.Text` is explicitly documented as "Empty means the provider settled nothing, which must not be read as 'the streamed text was wrong'" (`ports/chat.go`), and the ACP `settleOpenItems` path emits completions carrying the accumulated text only sometimes. Keep `current?.text` when the completion supplies no replacement, and add an empty-completion regression. The durable path has the same issue: `SettleAssistantMessage` at `controller.go:2634` passes `event.Text` straight through and the SQL does an unconditional `SET text = ?`.

Non-blocking coverage gap: `fresh := event.ProviderEventID == "" || event.ProviderEventFresh` means any harness that stamps a `ProviderEventID` without also setting the new `ProviderEventFresh` flag is treated as a replay and never previewed. Only the ACP adapter was updated to set the flag; `unrealagent` (`protocol.go:51`) sets `ProviderEventID` on every event, so that harness gets no live text at all, and worse, line 132 clears the whole journal on each such delta. Confirm which harnesses are expected to preview and document or gate the fallback, rather than silently disabling the feature for them.

Non-blocking / behavior note: `readLiveSnapshot` takes `projectionGate` around the durable read, so a snapshot request now blocks behind an in-flight projection write. That is the intended consistency mechanism (the tests assert a cancelled snapshot returns `DeadlineExceeded`), but it means a stalled SQLite write stalls the UI's durable refresh even though live text keeps streaming. Worth calling out explicitly in the PR body as a deliberate trade-off, since it is the failure mode the change is meant to mitigate.

**[P1 / blocking] Version 0167 collides with a migration already shipped on `main`.** `main` now ships `0167_allow_opencode_v2_harness.sql` (ledger `167: "0167_allow_opencode_v2_harness.sql"`), so this entry and file claim the same number. `TestMigrationVersionLedger` fails on the duplicate (`goose` also refuses to start on two files claiming one version), and `gh` reports the PR as `DIRTY` with the conflict exactly in this file. This branch is based on `381f563`, 20 commits behind `main`, so the PR body claim "Based on current main" is not true.

Please rebase onto current `main`, renumber the Pi migration to the next free version (`>= 0171`), and update every reference: this ledger entry, `openMigratedDatabaseCopy(t, 166)`, `upTo`/`downTo` in `migrate_pi_usage_test.go`, and any expected-version assertions. Since none of `0167_allow_opencode_v2_harness`/`0168`/`0169`/`0170` touch the usage tables, a straight renumber should work, but re-run the migration tests against the real head.

**[P2] The explicit `usage` entry type is still dropped, undercounting Pi totals.** Pi has a first-class `UsageEntry` (`{"type":"usage","kind":"cache_warm","provider":...,"model":...,"usage":{...}}`) that is deliberately hidden from the conversation tree but *does* contribute to session token and cost totals. The upstream canonical logic treats it as a model-attributed bucket (`entry.type === "usage"` → key `` `${entry.provider}/${entry.model}` ``), and the docs say "Consumers should treat unknown `kind` values as normal usage rather than rejecting them."

This parser handles only assistant, toolResult, compaction, and branch_summary, so every `usage` entry (e.g. cache warming) is silently skipped. That undercounts reported usage for a format the PR otherwise claims to fully normalize. Please add a `native.Type == "usage"` case using `provider`/`model` + `native.Usage` (the top-level `Usage` field already exists in `piSessionRecord`) and cover it in `pi_parser_test.go`.

Source: [session-format.md](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/session-format.md) (UsageEntry) and [usage-totals.ts](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/src/core/usage-totals.ts).

**[P2] `reconcilePiPath` swallows all validation errors, not just "not a Pi path".** `validateSourcePath` failing for any reason (transient stat/permission/root-resolution error, cancellation, an actual attribution mismatch) is converted to `nil`. Watch notifications legitimately target other providers, but a genuine failure here becomes invisible: no error surfaces, no `LastErrorCode` is recorded, and the source stays in `discovering` with no signal to the operator. Consider narrowing the swallow to the specific "path is not under a Pi root" condition (e.g. check `pathWithinRoot` first, as `ReconcilePath` already does) and returning other errors.

Also note this `nolint:nilerr` pattern means a canceled `ctx` inside `readPiSessionMeta` returns `ok=false` and the function silently reports success, which conflicts with the cancellation-propagation intent of the rest of this change.

Low severity — probe/predicate mismatch. This uses `NextQueuedTurn` as the "is there a queue" probe, but that query excludes rows with `promotion_started_at IS NOT NULL`, whereas `CancelQueuedTurns` (below) selects purely by `requested_at <= cutoff` and would cancel such a row. In practice `sendMu` serializes this against `PromoteQueuedTurn`, so no promotion can be in flight here and the mismatch is not reachable. Worth a one-line comment, or a probe that mirrors `CancelQueuedTurns`' predicate, so a future caller does not have to re-derive that invariant. Note also that if a promotion ever leaves a row stuck with `promotion_started_at` set (its `release()` failure is only logged), Stop would answer `ErrNoActiveTurn` for it and never clear it.

Minor — millisecond tie. `Date.parse(candidate.requestedAt) > heldAt` treats a fresh send whose `requestedAt` is exactly equal to the failed turn's `completedAt` as held, so its own dispatch window shows no Working bar. The daemon writes both from `c.now()`, and a send that lands in the same millisecond as the failure completion is plausible. Consider `>=` (with a note) or comparing by turn ordering rather than wall-clock.

**[P1] A cached `allow_always` survives a live downgrade.** This branch is what Auggie (bypass), Autohand and Kiro (auto/bypass) use. ACP defines `allow_always` as remember-the-choice, so after one automatic grant the provider stops sending permission requests for matching calls; a later switch to default or accept-edits only updates `conversation.permissionMode` in `applyTurnSettings` and never revokes the grant, so the tool runs with no prompt under a stricter displayed mode. `vibeacp` selects `allow_once` for auto/bypass for exactly this reason (a54c18b1f), and `cursoracp` is safe only because its validator refuses every live change involving auto/bypass. Either answer automatically with `allow_once` for the bindings that allow live changes, or reject a downgrade that would need provider-side grants cleared. The current test cannot catch a regression: `offered()` builds one option per kind, so it never models a provider that remembers an `allow_always`.

**[P2] This refuses a change Cline can apply without restarting.** With a nil mapper, `ApprovalFixedAtLaunch` compares the raw AO modes. But `configure` launches default and accept-edits identically (`--acp`), auto and bypass identically (`--acp --auto-approve true`), and `StandardPermissionPolicy()` resolves accept-edits per request from the conversation current mode. So default to accept-edits (and auto to bypass) fails the next turn with `ErrACPSetterUnsupported` and tells the user to restart Chat, even though the live session would enforce the new mode. Pass a `launchValue` that maps default/accept-edits to the empty string and auto/bypass to `auto` (the shape `gooseMode` already uses) and add transition tests for both pairs.

**[P2] This rewrites the shared `.kiro/agents/ao.json` with an empty `AgentConfig`.** `setKiroAgentDefaults` deletes `model` whenever `AgentConfig.Model` is empty and always overwrites `prompt`, so a TUI to Chat handoff silently drops the model the TUI path configured and replaces its `file://` prompt-file reference with the inline system prompt (`null` when the Chat launch has no system prompt). It also writes the standing prompt into the checkout instead of the session-private prompt directory used by the other bindings. Preserve the existing model and prompt reference when the Chat launch has nothing to change, or stop sharing one file between the two interfaces.

**[P2] The inherited permission map is replaced, not merged.** `existing` comes from the session env `KILO_CONFIG_CONTENT`, which can carry user-owned rules such as a `webfetch` deny; any non-default AO mode overwrites the whole map, so those deny/ask rules are lost with no error. The `agent` map just below is merged carefully; the permission map should be layered the same way, with AO entries winning only for the tools AO actually sets.

**[P3] The documented PATH fallback is unreachable when the CLI is missing.** This returns early on `plugin.ResolveBinary` failure, so a user who installed `autohand-acp` but not the `autohand` CLI gets `autohand-acp is not installed` even though the adapter is present. Resolve the adapter independently and keep the CLI only as the auth probe. `vibeacp.resolveVibeACPBinary` has the same shape.

Correction to the mechanism in my comment above (the gap itself is real; my explanation of *why* was wrong).

I traced `charmbracelet/x/ansi@v0.11.6` (`parser.go`, `parser/transition_table.go`) and `vt-go@v0.2.0` directly. An empty `Ps` does **not** dispatch as command `0`. `parseStringCmd` leaves `cmd == MissingCommand` (2147483647) when the first byte after the introducer is not a digit, and vt-go's `handleOsc` finds no handler for that command, so nothing title-related runs.

What actually leaks is command-independent: the parser terminates any OSC string at the first `0x9C` byte in the payload, because `OscStringState` dispatches on `0x9C`. So:

- `ESC ] ; plain title BEL` (no `0x9C`) → fully swallowed, no leak.
- `ESC ] ; ✳ title BEL` → `OSC cmd=2147483647 data=";\xe2"`, then `title` is printed as ground text → leak.
- Same for command `0`, `1`, `2`, C1 `0x9D`, and even malformed commands like `0X`.

So the premature-ST termination is the sole cause for every form; the command value only decides whether the filter strips the payload. Treating empty `Ps` as command 0 would still be a reasonable way to close this specific gap, but the justification is "make the filter cover every introducer spelling the parser accepts", not "the parser reads it as command 0".
