[P1] Preserve the old Chat generation until teardown completes. On a live Chat-to-Terminal switch, `setReviewerInterfaceMode` clears `controller_generation` before `launcher.Destroy(previousHandleID)` stops the old Chat controller. Its generation-fenced cleanup then returns `owned=false`, so in-flight reviewer turns and pending approval/user-input requests are never settled. Keep the old fence through teardown or settle the old controller before clearing it.

[P1] Roll back a failed deferred notification. In a mode-changing replacement the old pane has already been destroyed before this `Notify` call. If the prompt send fails, this branch destroys the replacement and fails the runs but never restores the previous review row or reviewer surface, leaving the database pointed at a destroyed replacement and losing the prior Chat conversation. Handle this failure with the same replacement rollback/recovery path.

[P2] Include the host in the reviewer draft scope. `ChatWorkspace` uses `draftOwner` as the full scope, so it overrides the host-qualified `uiSessionId` passed below. Because this owner is keyed only by `reviewId`, equal reviewer IDs on different hosts share composer drafts, tab order, and inspector state.

[P2] Invalidate the host-qualified review query on errors. For remote sessions `reviewsKey` is `["session-reviews", hostId, session.id]`, but this invalidates `["session-reviews", session.id]`, which does not match the remote cache. A failed remote trigger therefore leaves stale reviewer mode and run state visible.

[P1] Reconcile orphaned Chat work before the unavailable-Chat downgrade. This recovery branch changes the row to Terminal while `SetReviewInterfaceMode` now deliberately preserves `controller_generation` for the explicit Chat→Terminal teardown path, but it never stops a controller or calls `CleanupOwnedReviewControllerWork`. After a daemon restart, `previousRuns` can contain a running reviewer turn or pending approval/input from the dead Chat controller; `RestoreTerminal` starts an idle pane and the stale generation remains in the row, so that work stays live forever and automatic review reconciliation can remain blocked. Settle/fail the old review work before downgrading (or clear the generation after proving the controller is gone); apply the same treatment in `restoreReviewerLocked`.

[P2] Scope the pending interface choice by host as well as session. `pendingReviewerInterfaceMode` stores only `sessionId`, but `ReviewsSection` stays mounted when `hostId` changes and this UI already host-qualifies session keys because IDs can overlap. A mode selected on remote host A can therefore be sent to local host B for the same session ID, and the old mutation's success/error handler can clear the new host's pending choice. Include `hostId` in the pending key and reset predicates.

P2: This component can stay mounted while the selected session changes, but `dismissed` is initialized only once from the original `dismissalKey`. If a user dismisses one session’s startup error and switches to another session with a failed cue, this stale `true` hides the new banner and suppresses its toast. Reload dismissal state when `dismissalKey` changes, or key the component by session and run.

P2: If this release callback fails (for example, while delivering the opening prompt or queued TUI messages), the error is only logged, then the deferred cleanup clears `DeliveryHeld`. Later terminal input can bypass the undelivered rows, leaving them stuck until restart recovery drains them. Please preserve/retry a drain path or surface a recoverable delivery failure before releasing the hold.

**P1 — A persisted held cue can prevent the daemon from starting after restart.** For a committed Chat session, this runs during `ReconcileStartupSafety`, before `ReconcileBackground` reattaches its Chat controller. `releasePersistedStartupCueDelivery` drains the chat queue, and `DrainQueued` returns `ErrNoController` until that controller exists. The error propagates out of startup safety and `daemon.Run` aborts before serving. Could recovery retain the hold here and defer draining until after controller reattachment?

**P2 — Canceling setup may leave its command running.** This assigns the terminal handle only to the worker's local `run`; it is not persisted before the poll loop. `CancelStartupCue` reads the persisted run, so its close-terminal branch is skipped while the command is running. It then marks the cue cancelled and releases queued input, but the worker's `commandCtx` is not cancelled by this endpoint. The setup command can therefore continue modifying the worktree after normal session input resumes. Please persist/cancel the active terminal before releasing delivery.

`lastFocusedViewId` is set whenever the panel is shown (`= viewId` at ~L1938) and on page focus, but it's only cleared when the panel is hidden or destroyed (or via `forgetLastFocusedPanel`). It is **not** cleared when the AO window loses OS focus or is minimized.

So the main use case for this feature (the user had the session's Browser panel open, walks away, and picks up the phone) puts every phone tap and scroll here: `BROWSER_REMOTE_READ_ONLY: Desktop browser control is active`. The phone can watch but never control until someone hides the panel on the desktop.

Suggestion: gate on actual focus, e.g. `options.mainWindow.isFocused() && lastFocusedViewId === session.viewId` (plus `!isMinimized()`), or track a short "recent desktop input" timestamp instead of last-focused state.

Follow-up to the sticky-error fix: recovery now depends on a *later frame*, but `Page.startScreencast` only emits frames when the page repaints. A rejected input (`BROWSER_REMOTE_READ_ONLY` from the comment above, or `BROWSER_REMOTE_NOT_VIEWED`) doesn't change the page, so on a static page the overlay covers a healthy stream indefinitely. While `status !== "open"`, the PanResponder is also disabled, so the only way out is "Check again", which tears down and re-reserves the lease.

Suggestion: split host errors into fatal (capture unavailable or host disconnected → overlay) and per-command rejections (read-only, invalid input → transient banner/toast, keep status `open`). The broker could also tag command-failure errors from `dispatchControl` so the phone can tell them apart.

(Likely, please verify on a device) `nativeEvent.locationX/Y` are relative to the view that was actually touched (the gesture *target*), not the view that owns the PanResponder. Once a frame is showing, that target is the absolutely-positioned `<Image style={frameRect}>`, so `locationX/Y` are already image-relative. `normalizedPoint()` then subtracts `rect.left/top` a second time.

In the common case (portrait phone, landscape desktop), `rect.top` is large, so taps in the top band of the image return `null` and are silently dropped, and the rest land offset upward by `rect.top`.

Simplest fix: `pointerEvents="none"` on the `Image` (and the "Waiting…" overlay) so the viewport is always the target. Alternatively, use `pageX/Y` minus the viewport's measured origin.

The per-session lease is held until this handler returns, but this socket has no ping/heartbeat (unlike the terminal WebSocket's `heartbeatLoop`), and the phone doesn't close the stream when the app backgrounds. Some cases that leave a stale lease:
- iOS suspends the app (TCP stays up with a zero window, so writes just stall).
- The phone switches Wi-Fi ↔ cellular (no FIN).
- The app is killed.

On a static page nothing is written, so TCP keepalive (~2.5 min) is the only thing that eventually notices. When the user reopens Preview, the **same phone** gets 409 `BROWSER_CONTROL_IN_USE`, and the fallback copy tells them another phone is controlling it. Meanwhile the desktop keeps capturing.

Suggestions: (a) add a `c.Ping` heartbeat like `terminal/manager.go`'s, and/or (b) let a new authenticated connection preempt the existing lease instead of failing with 409, since all paired phones share one credential. That would also fix the fast Browser ↔ App tab-toggle race, where the reconnect can beat the old socket's release. On mobile, closing the stream on `AppState` `background` would help too.

When the session's browser is destroyed on the desktop, the live stream is dropped silently, with no `live.sink.error(...)`. The broker still has the subscription and the WebSocket stays open, so the phone keeps showing the last frame as if it were live. The next tap then hits `ensureSessionReady` (which may recreate the browser) and fails with `BROWSER_REMOTE_NOT_VIEWED`.

Suggestion: call `live.sink.error("BROWSER_SESSION_CLOSED", ...)` before clearing it, and have the phone treat that as fatal.

Hardening: `stop` ignores `control.streamId` and stops whatever stream the session has. The broker sends `stop` for the old stream ID *after* releasing its lock, so if a new `Subscribe` for the same session ever sends `start` first, this `stop` would kill the new stream (the phone would sit on "Waiting for the desktop browser…" with no error). Today the exclusive lease plus `defer` ordering (`sub.Close()` before `release()`) happens to prevent that.

Cheap fix: `host.stopLiveStream(sessionId, control.streamId)` and no-op when `session.live.streamId` doesn't match.

Consider defaulting to `"app"` when a preview exists and the browser stream fails with `BROWSER_REMOTE_DISABLED`/handshake error, or remembering the last-used tab.

[P1] Preserve a newer desktop opt-out while loading the saved preference

If the pending storage read returns `null` after the connected desktop has already reported `optedOut: true`, this call applies `false` over that newer state. `setOptedOut(false)` then calls SDK `optIn()` and removes the saved marker, so subsequent events are sent while the desktop remains opted out. Finish preference restoration before adopting live desktop state, or prevent an older restore from overwriting it. Add a startup test that defers the marker read until after a desktop opt-out is applied.

[P2] Update identity properties before emitting identify

The cleanup below runs after `client.identify()`. When the phone switches from user A to user B, the SDK still has A's `ao_cloud_user_id` and `github_actor` registered at this call. [PostHog 4.62.0 builds the identify payload from those current properties](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-js/blob/45755858b2844df60d788277a2d82b9b05048d78/packages/core/src/posthog-core.ts#L345-L390), so the queued `$identify` for B carries A's attributes. Later unregister/register calls only fix subsequent events. [P2] Ignore hand-off responses from an invalidated daemon

`invalidate()` sets `pushed` to false, but an already-running `flush()` can undo that change here. B's ready transition then skips the replay and its new identity never receives the cloud user. The added restart test waits for the first request to finish before invalidating, so it misses this case. Track a generation across invalidation and check it before accepting a response, with a deferred-response test for this ordering.

**Closed-lid wake gets turned on without the user asking.** `settings.lidClosed` defaults to `true` on lid-capable Macs (`service.go` Settings default), and `?? true` applies while state hasn't loaded. So flipping "Keep awake" in Connect Mobile (or the sidebar) starts `{scope: "ao", lidClosed: true}` even when the "Keep awake with lid closed" switch shows off — the Mac can stay awake with the lid shut in a bag. With the settings page removed there's also no UI left to change `settings.lidClosed`.

On Macs where the lid capability is unavailable (or before state loads), the forced `true` makes Start fail with "closed-lid wake is unavailable", so a switch that used to work now errors.

Suggest defaulting to `false` here and only passing `true` when the user has explicitly opted in via a visible control.

`invalidateQueries` only refetches *active* queries. If Connect Mobile isn't mounted but `mobile-status` is still cached (e.g. Settings prefetched it), the cache keeps `keepAwake.enabled: true` after this POST succeeds. Once `intent` resets to `null`, `on = legacyOn = true` and the sidebar button snaps back to pressed; further clicks keep re-POSTing until the cache is GC'd ~5 min later.

Consider `cache.setQueryData(mobileStatusQueryKey, ...)` to optimistically clear `keepAwake.enabled`, or `invalidateQueries({ queryKey, refetchType: "all" })`.

`legacyOn` only reads whatever happens to be in the query cache and never fetches. After an app restart (or once the cache is GC'd), a mobile keep-awake flag saved before upgrade is invisible: the sidebar shows off while the mobile bridge still holds caffeinate, and turning the toggle off never clears the flag because `legacyOn` is false. That defeats the goal in the doc comment above ("cannot keep the Mac awake with no switch left to turn it off").

A `useQuery` on `mobileStatusQueryKey` (perhaps with a long `staleTime` so it doesn't add polling) would make this reliable.

The old control used `disabled={!supported || awake.busy}`; this drops the busy guard. Fast double-click: click 1 → `set(true)` with the start POST pending; click 2 → `set(!on)` = `set(false)` using the stale empty `sessions` closure, so nothing is ended and its `finally` resets `intent` to `null`. Click 1's start then completes and the Mac stays awake indefinitely even though the last click meant off.

Suggest `disabled={!stay.supported || stay.busy}` (or an in-flight ref inside `set`).

This test pins down that the toggle deliberately ignores session-scoped sessions — but this PR also removes the per-session "For this session" control and the Stay Awake settings page. Users who upgrade with an existing session-scoped session, an automation rule, or a timed session have no remaining UI to end it or turn the rule off; caffeinate keeps running while the sidebar button shows off.

Either keep a way to see/end those (or migrate/clear them on upgrade), or have the toggle reflect and end all active sessions.

Every sibling footer row gets `tabIndex={isCollapsed ? -1 : 0}`, but `<AwakeControl />` doesn't, so with the offcanvas sidebar collapsed (footer `aria-hidden`) Tab can land on the invisible coffee button and Space toggles Stay Awake unseen. Could `AwakeControl` accept and forward a `tabIndex` prop?

Nit/fragility: the retry path keys off the substring `"safety stop"` in the daemon's English error text. Rewording that message in `service.go` would silently break resume-and-retry. Exposing the stop reason in `AwakeState` (or letting the daemon's Start handle the explicit rearm) would be sturdier.

`on` can be true purely because of the legacy mobile flag, which never makes the awake service `active`. In that case `starting` stays true forever and the button reports `aria-busy="true"` indefinitely. Maybe base this on `intent === true && !awake.state?.active` instead.

The inline `subscribe` is a new function every render, so `useSyncExternalStore` unsubscribes/resubscribes to the whole `QueryCache` each render, and `getSnapshot` re-runs on every cache event app-wide (including the 5s polls) — on a component that's always mounted. Wrapping `subscribe` in `useCallback([cache])` fixes the churn (or this goes away if you switch to `useQuery` per the comment above).

[P1] Establish that the other owner is inactive before reclaiming

Being outside this instance's managed root with the same suffix does not prove that a worktree is orphaned. For example, run production and an isolated AO development instance against the same project on the same volume: their deterministic orchestrator paths have identical project/orchestrator/prefix suffixes. Spawning the orchestrator in the second instance now classifies the first instance's live, unlocked, clean worktree as an orphan and deletes its working directory. Neither the branch nor this path check carries any liveness/ownership evidence, and normal AO worktrees are not locked. Please retain the conflict unless there is positive evidence that the prior owner is inactive, or make reclamation an explicit user action. Add a regression case with two active data roots; the existing integration test uses two Workspace objects but assumes the first is abandoned.

[P1] Preserve ignored local files before automatic removal

Omitting `--force` does not make this automatic deletion lossless. A prior worktree with a tracked ignore rule for `.env` and a local `.env` containing credentials is clean to Git; `git worktree remove` succeeds and recursively deletes that file, and checking out the branch at the new root cannot restore it. Git's `check_clean_worktree` uses ordinary `status --porcelain`, which omits ignored files, before deleting the directory (https://github.com/git/git/blob/master/builtin/worktree.c#L1271-L1329). This is a new automatic removal on spawn, so the caller has not requested discarding those local files. Please move/adopt the worktree, preserve the local files, or refuse automatic reclamation when non-reconstructible ignored content is present. Add a real-Git regression test with an ignored `.env`; the untracked `scratch.txt` test does not exercise this case.

[P2] Treat a different Windows volume as outside the managed root

`pathWithin` calls `filepath.Rel`, which returns an error for paths on different Windows volumes; this guard therefore returns false before the suffix match. With the old registration at `D:/ao-cc-lab-data/worktrees/<project>/orchestrator/<prefix>-orchestrator` and the current managed root at `C:/Users/<user>/.ao/data/worktrees`, even a genuinely abandoned, clean, unlocked worktree keeps producing the original 409. This is especially relevant to the D: lab-root example in #6918. Handle unequal volumes as outside-root rather than an unclassifiable path, while retaining the appropriate ownership checks, and add a Windows cross-volume classification test. Both new integration roots are under one `t.TempDir`, so Windows CI does not cover this.

No directory is deleted on spawn, which removes both the liveness and the ignored-file concerns.

[P1] Apply the handoff policy to the actual agent open route

The new guard only covers navigateEntry, but execute(..., 'open', ...) below calls runNative('open', ...) directly, which sends navigation through the agent-browser CDP bridge rather than this function. Programmatic Page.navigate is not an in-page will-navigate event, so opening accounts.google.com or a configured SSO host through ao browser open can still load it inside the panel and returns ordinary navigation state instead of the documented handoff. Check the normalized URL in the actual agent open dispatch before invoking the native runtime, and return the handoff state there; cover execute('open') rather than only the browser:navigate IPC in the tests.

[P2] Preserve the handoff notice across navigation-state refreshes

externalHandoff is only written into entry.state here, while readNavState reconstructs its result from driver().page() and never carries this field forward. Consequently the next pushNavState erases the notice and Open again button. In particular, preventing an HTTP redirect ends the load, and wireNavEvents handles did-stop-loading by calling pushNavState; loadEntry also does that for the aborted load. The redirect handoff therefore loses its notice as soon as cancellation finishes. Persist the handoff separately or preserve it in readNavState until an explicit subsequent navigation clears it, and cover the complete redirect/cancellation event sequence.

[P2] Strip the current application name from the user agent

main.ts already calls app.setName('Orchestrator.inc') in packaged builds (and 'Orchestrator.inc (dev)' in development). Electron builds app.userAgentFallback from that application name with spaces removed, so the real app token is Orchestrator.inc/<version> or Orchestrator.inc(dev)/<version>, neither of which this expression matches. Electron/ is removed but the embedding app remains advertised, violating the app-token-free UA acceptance criterion. Derive the token from the configured app name or explicitly handle the actual production and development names, and test those fallback strings rather than only the historical AgentOrchestrator token.

[P1] Redact the nested handoff URL before returning it to agents

The handoff branch passes navState through agentNavState, but that helper only sanitizes the top-level url, title and error; its ...state spread leaves externalHandoff.url untouched. More importantly, after a person clicks an OAuth link containing sensitive parameters, the new readNavState preservation carries that human-originated handoff URL into a later ordinary agent open response, because runNative('open') does not clear it through navigateEntry. Apply sanitizeBrowserURL to externalHandoff.url at the agent response boundary while keeping the original URL privately available for shell.openExternal/Open again, and cover this nested field in the redaction tests.

[P1] Bind screenshots to the session-owned tab

A deterministic concurrent reproduction captured tab 2 for both sessions; use a tab-bound capture operation, or serialize window activation/capture and reject target changes so pixels from a different tab cannot be returned.

[P1] Enforce site policy on the selected frame

[P1] Honor cancellation before dispatching more trusted input

`Stop all agents` aborts the in-flight controllers, but the trusted-input queue and dispatch loop never receive their signal. Pausing the initial mouse movement, aborting, and resuming still dispatched both `mousePressed` and `mouseReleased` after cancellation and returned `clicked: true`; propagate the signal through queued attachment, paced movement, and dispatch, checking cancellation before each event and safely releasing any held input.

[P2] Accumulate every ancestor offset for nested frames

Selecting an outer frame and then its child succeeds, but `point()` adds only the immediate parent's offset even though trusted pointer events use top-level coordinates. With outer offset `(100,200)`, inner offset `(20,30)`, and target `(10,15)`, the reproduction clicked `(30,45)` instead of `(130,245)`; retain and accumulate the complete frame ancestry, or reject unsupported nesting before dispatching input.

[P2] Keep selector waits pending while the element is hidden

A `querySelector()` result is connected, so `visible || found.isConnected` immediately satisfies the selector wait for an existing `display:none` element. The panel's pinned agent-browser runtime defaults selector waits to visible, so Chrome mode can advance before an element can be used; apply equivalent dimensions/display/visibility checks instead of treating DOM attachment as visibility.

[P2] Preserve Windows registrations owned by another data directory

[P2] Keep supervised live agents deliverable when their prompt contains `<defunct>`

This new liveness check uses `procmem.Snapshot`, whose parser drops any process row whose full command contains the literal `<defunct>` (`internal/procmem/procmem.go:86`). A supervised native launch keeps its child argv in the supervisor's command, and Codex/Claude launch prompts can be passed in argv. An initial task such as `explain <defunct> processes` therefore removes the live supervisor from the parsed tree. The probe remains `unknown/workload_unconfirmed`, and subsequent `Manager.Send` deliveries are rejected with `ErrRuntimeProbeInconclusive` even though the agent is healthy. Raw terminal input still works.

Reproduced on macOS at `9a78a80fdfe44c79e42326fb1bba2c51b7117abd` using a temporary test with the existing native supervisor fixture:

1. Create a real native PTY host with argv `[testExecutable, "agent-process", "supervise", "--session", id, "--launch", "launch-1", "--", "/bin/sh", "-c", supervisedWindowAgent, "explain <defunct> processes"]` and the fixture's ready/input/report/release file environment.
2. Wait for the agent's ready file; verify `IsChildAlive` returns `true`.
3. Call `SendInput(handle, "healthy\r")` and verify `healthy` appears in the agent's input log.
4. Probe the matching session/handle/generation three times. All three return `{Liveness:unknown Reason:workload_unconfirmed}` instead of `alive`.

Suggested fix: use actual process state or a dedicated managed-child liveness probe, rather than the memory parser's command-substring zombie heuristic. Preserve the existing startup/previous-observation rule and treat incomplete process reads as inconclusive. Add a regression test with literal `<defunct>` in the launch prompt.

[P2] Do not assume missing supervision metadata means a direct-child agent

This intentional compatibility default leaves #6485 unfixed for preserved native sessions created before the upgrade. Their registry entries already contain `LaunchID` but lack the new `supervised` field, so adoption sets `sess.supervised=false`. `ProbeFencedRuntime` then skips the managed-child check and returns `alive/exact_match` for a supervisor whose agent has exited. `requireLiveDeliveryTarget` accepts that result, so the new send guard cannot prevent the original false success on these sessions. Sessions deliberately survive daemon shutdown and are adopted on the next boot.

Reproduced on macOS at `9a78a80fdfe44c79e42326fb1bba2c51b7117abd` with the existing real native supervisor fixture:

1. Start `startSupervisedWindow(..., true)` and wait for its agent to be ready.
2. Rewrite its registry entry with `Supervised=false` using `ptyregistry.Register`, preserving `LaunchID`, host PID and address. Because the field is `omitempty`, this serializes the pre-upgrade JSON layout without `supervised`.
3. Exit the managed agent and hold its supervisor at the fixture's exit-report barrier.
4. Construct a fresh `Runtime` with the same run-file path, matching daemon adoption.
5. The recovered runtime's matching fenced probe returns `{Liveness:alive Reason:exact_match}`. `SendInput` returns `nil`, but the exited agent's input log contains no new message.

The temporary test `TestReviewLegacySupervisorRegistryAfterUpgrade` failed its assertion that this target must not be reported alive; it was removed after verification. The probe/write results above were measured directly; acceptance by `Manager.Send` follows from its `FencedAlive` branch.

Suggested fix: distinguish unknown supervision metadata from a positively known unsupervised launch, then safely recognize the existing AO supervisor or refuse delivery as inconclusive. This needs explicit serialization of known `false` (or equivalent tri-state metadata), since the current `omitempty` also omits false for newly created unsupervised entries. Retain genuine direct-child compatibility and add an adoption test using the old JSON layout. This is an incomplete fix, not a newly introduced regression.

[P1] `hasQueued` is global carry-over state: any later `UserPromptSubmit` hook consumes the last queued command, even when its `parentUuid` does not point to that queued record. Intervening attachments or a malformed/missing hook can therefore associate stale text with an unrelated submission and let checkpoint verification accept the wrong prompt. Track the queued record UUID and require the hook parent to match it (clearing state when the chain diverges), with tests for intervening and broken-parent records.

[P2] This reuses `projectDetails`, but that CLI mirror is already incomplete relative to `projectsvc.Project`: it omits `folderMissing`, workspace `gitStatus`, `config.preRemove`, and `AgentConfig.effort`. Please either complete the mirror (including nested types) or preserve the project subtree as raw JSON for this response.

[P2] The confirmation happens before any daemon request, so the user is asked to approve a write without seeing the validated current-to-proposed diff. This contradicts the command contract added in this PR and also means invalid input prompts before failing. Please perform the dry-run/validation request first, display its changes, then confirm and issue the real write.

[P2] Writing the interactive prompt to stdout makes `ao project update ... --json` emit prompt text before the JSON document, so consumers cannot parse the output as JSON. Route the prompt and abort message to stderr, or require `--yes` whenever `--json` is used.

[P1] These migration IDs are already shipped on current `main`: `0213_session_stale_binary.sql` and `0214_app_settings_version_refresh.sql` (with `0215_session_harness_releases.sql` after them). Reusing 0213/0214 makes the branch conflicting and can cause Goose to treat unrelated schema work as already applied. Regenerate both migrations with `npm run migration:create -- <name>`, append the generated IDs to `shippedMigrations`, and update the legacy-history repair/tests to target those new IDs.

[P1] `0202_allow_memcode_harness.sql` is already shipped on current `main`, so this migration collides with an unrelated applied Goose version. The repository now also requires timestamped migration IDs created through `npm run migration:create`. Regenerate this PR's four migrations with fresh IDs, update `shippedMigrations`, and adjust the migration/history fixtures before rebasing; otherwise existing databases can skip the dreaming schema while recording the version as applied.

[P2] This is one service-wide mutex, and it stays held through database reads, a provider account refresh, hibernation wake, and a retry with a 90-second timeout. One slow session therefore serializes every other due auto-resume and also blocks `SetTurnAutoResume`, so a user cannot cancel another pending retry during that interval despite the method's stated contract. Keep the mutex around the retry-map/consent coordination only, or use per-turn/session serialization while rechecking consent immediately before dispatch.

[P1] The read-only guarantee is bypassable because `SessionID` is trusted from the request body. AO's primary loopback API is intentionally unauthenticated, and an ordinary agent can call it directly (or unset `AO_SESSION_ID`) with an empty `sessionId`; the service then treats the write as a user edit and skips the dream-only checks. Do not infer user authority from an omitted client field. The daemon needs trusted caller provenance/capability for in-session writes while preserving the existing unauthenticated loopback listener contract.

[P2] Once the reset time arrives, this hides the auto-resume toggle even if `usageLimit.autoResume` is still armed. The daemon deliberately preserves consent and retries transient failures, so at the exact point a wake/retry may be running or backing off the user loses the only Cancel auto-resume control and sees a separate manual Resume button instead. Keep the cancellation action visible while `autoResume` remains true (including after the deadline), and distinguish the pending/retrying state from an unarmed ready state.

[P1] Even after identifying a real dreaming session, this authorizes it solely by the automation purpose. There is no check that the automation/session belongs to the `projectID` being edited, so a dream for project A can write project B's standing instructions by calling that route with B's ID. Permit global instructions only as explicitly intended, and for project-scoped instructions require the target project to match the dreaming automation/session project; cover the cross-project denial.

[P1] If this ACK fails after `projectEvent` has committed a `turn.completed`, this branch detaches before `afterProject` reports idle and drains the queued prompt. On reconnect the same provider-event ID is already in the durable archive, so `ProjectProviderEvent` returns `projected=false` and `afterProject` is skipped again; publishing the replacement controller does not independently drain that queue. The queued user turn can therefore remain stuck indefinitely in exactly the ACK-loss scenario this PR is designed to recover. Please reconcile these post-commit lifecycle effects on ACK failure/reconnect (or make replay of a committed completion trigger the idempotent drain), with a regression test for commit-success + ACK-failure + queued input.

[P2] This marks every stopped/failed account-switch turn as handing its actions to `TurnOutcome`, but the render below intentionally suppresses `TurnOutcome` when `group.accountSwitched` is true. As a result the final assistant message loses copy/rollback, the tool-only fallback is also suppressed, and there is no replacement action row. Exclude account-switch endings from `endsWithOutcome` or render the actions beside the account-switch marker so those turns keep the same recovery controls.

[P2] `MsgTerminalInput` is not exclusively a viewer signal. `clientSendMessage` and `clientSendInput` each open a fresh write-only connection whose first frame is `MsgTerminalInput`, never read terminal data, and close after writing. Classifying those connections as viewers queues and writes up to the full 4 MiB replay on every automated send/input, reintroducing the replay amplification and back-pressure this change is intended to remove. Please give real attaches an explicit viewer hello and keep fire-and-forget input connections input-only, or otherwise distinguish those two call paths in the protocol.

[P2] Auto-follow is cancelled for pointer use, but not for keyboard interaction. A keyboard user can focus and activate a disclosure inside this window; because `following.current` remains true, the resulting resize (or the next streamed item) immediately calls `followEnd()` and pulls the viewport away from what they opened. Add a keyboard/focus-based takeover path (for example capture focus/keydown from interactive descendants) and cover it alongside the wheel/pointer behavior.

[P2] Overriding `HOME` is not sufficient to isolate Kimi when the daemon inherited `KIMI_CODE_HOME` from the user. The current official installer computes `KIMI_HOME_DIR=${KIMI_CODE_HOME:-$HOME/.kimi-code}` and writes its region marker there, while `RunInstall` appends these overrides to the full daemon environment. A user-defined `KIMI_CODE_HOME` therefore sends this supposedly private install back into the user's real Kimi data. Explicitly set `KIMI_CODE_HOME` to a directory under this release (and cover an inherited value in the recipe test).

[P2] Splitting one newline-free logical line into 64 KiB entries changes `Tail(n)` from a line-based API into an entry-based API. For example, after a 130 KiB line, `Tail(1)` returns only the final 64 KiB chunk rather than the last logical line; `Snapshot()` also starts treating earlier chunks of the still-in-progress line as completed even though its contract says the partial line is excluded. That can truncate terminal inspection at arbitrary byte boundaries. Please keep byte eviction metadata separate from logical line boundaries, or teach `Tail`/`Snapshot` to reassemble chunked lines while retaining the byte cap.

[P3] The comment says the key is stable by label kind, but `task:${task}` includes the task text. Every tool/task label change therefore changes the key, remounts the span, and replays `.chat-live-label`'s entrance animation. Use a stable `task` key here; only the text content should update in place.

[P2] The managed official installers still execute in the daemon's inherited working directory. Goose's official script downloads `$FILE` and writes extraction-error logs as relative paths before cleaning them up, so a desktop daemon whose cwd is read-only will fail the update; a failed run can also leave vendor artifacts in whatever directory launched AO. Run installer scripts from their private `jobDir` (or add an explicit trusted working directory to the install command) so the managed-install boundary covers cwd as well as HOME/PATH.

[P2] This safety decision is keyed only by harness target, but advisory ownership can be derived from the binary's actual Homebrew receipt and may produce a different cask package for that target. In that case any Claude/Copilot/Droid cask is treated as a self-contained single binary and allowed to update beside live sessions, even though only the specific audited casks have that layout. Key this allowlist by the exact cask package (or carry an audited-layout flag from the selected plan) before returning `safe`.

**This polls `/api/v1/mobile/status` every 5s on every Mac for as long as the app is open**, because the sidebar's `AwakeControl` is always mounted with `enabled = true`. Before this PR, Connect Mobile only polled while pairing was pending (`mobileStatusRefetchInterval` → 2s, otherwise `false`), so steady state was no polling at all.

`BridgeService.Status()` isn't cheap: it reads the mobile config from disk, enumerates network interfaces, waits on `awaitBootTunnel()`, and when secure pairing is on calls `queryTS()` → `tailscale status --json` (3s timeout). So users with secure pairing get a `tailscale` process spawned every 5s indefinitely.

A couple of related points:
- There's no error backoff here, unlike `useAwake` (which drops to 60s while failing).
- `supported` now requires `mobile.data`, so the desktop Stay Awake button is disabled until mobile status loads, which at daemon startup waits on the boot tunnel.

Since the mutation already writes the authoritative POST response into the cache (`setQueryData`) and Connect Mobile has its own polling, could this drop the interval (fetch on mount/focus, maybe with a long `staleTime`), or use something much longer like 60s? **The button can show "on" while nothing is keeping the Mac awake.** `desktopOn` (and `on` at line 89) counts open sessions and armed rules, not whether the daemon is actually holding wake:

Failed/cancelled notices always tell the worker to request another review, and the updated worker prompt says the same. But several endings are not reasons to re-trigger: `SupersedeStaleRunningReviewRuns` marks the old run `failed` with "superseded by a review trigger for a newer commit" exactly when a new pass for the new head is already running, and `cancelled by user` is a deliberate user stop. In both cases the worker gets "AO review done: failed/cancelled ... Request another review" and will likely run `ao review trigger` again (re-requesting a review the user cancelled, or racing the pass already in flight). Either skip the notice for superseded runs (e.g. do not mark them pending, or drop them at delivery when a newer run for the same PR is running/complete) or word those cases distinctly ("superseded; a review of <newer head> is already running" / "cancelled by the user; do not re-request unless asked"), and add tests for both.

The 24h window is not enforced on GitHub: `github.Provider.ListPRsByRepo` sends it as `since` to `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls`, and that endpoint has no `since` parameter, so it is ignored and the loop pages through every open PR in the repository (100 per page) on each no-PR trigger. That contradicts the doc comment / PR description ("never pages through a repository full open-PR list") and, on a repo with many open PRs, can eat the 10s `prRefreshTimeout` so the lookup silently fails. Use a branch-filtered query instead (GitHub `pulls?head=<owner>:<branch>&state=open`, GitLab `source_branch=`), e.g. a small optional `ListPRsByBranch` provider method, or at minimum stop paging once results are older than the cutoff (list is sorted by updated desc) and fix the comment.

**The inactive tooltip can blame an unrelated closed-lid problem.** `awake.state.reason` isn't only a stop reason. In `Service.Status()` it falls back in order to `s.reason` → `host.RecoveryReason()` → the **lid controller's** `lidReason` (anything except `setup_needed`).

On a Mac where closed-lid wake isn't available, that lid reason is set permanently: `LidAwake.status` returns `l.reason` when `!l.supported` (e.g. `unsupported`, `isolated_data_dir`), and `KeepAwake.LidStatus` returns `helper_missing` when there's no lid controller. So whenever the button is inactive for a different reason, such as an armed rule waiting for its condition, `AwakeControl.tsx:24` looks it up under `mobile.keepAwake.lidReason.*` and the tooltip reads e.g.:

> Stay Awake is configured but inactive. The desktop wake helper is missing. Update or restart the AO desktop app. Click to turn off.

Closed-lid wake was never requested, so the message points the user at the wrong problem.

Related:
- Awake-only reasons like `observation_unavailable` and `persistence_failed` have no translation, so they fall back to raw lowercase text mid-sentence ("…but inactive. observation unavailable Click to turn off.").
- The reused `lidReason.low_battery` string hardcodes "below 10%", but the awake service stops at `Settings.StopBatteryPercent` (10–90). A user who changed it before upgrading, with no settings page left to see it, gets the wrong number.

Suggestion: only surface `reason` when `awake.state.paused` is set and it's a safety-stop reason (`low_battery`, `critical_heat`, `battery_unknown`), otherwise use the generic inactive tooltip. Alternatively, add Stay Awake–specific strings instead of reusing the mobile lid ones. A test with `state.reason = "helper_missing"` and an armed, unmatched rule would pin it down.

**Install plan isn't pinned to the only version Chat accepts.** `planBrew(target, "docker-agent")` installs whatever the current formula is, but `validateInitialize` in `dockeragentacp/driver.go` only accepts exactly `v1.150.0`. Once Homebrew moves past 1.150.0, AO's own Install button installs a binary that the first Chat turn rejects with "docker agent native ACP requires tested v1.150.0", and AO gives the user no way to get the qualified version.

Either pin the install (a versioned formula, or the manual standalone binary only), or relax the initialize check to a tested range.

**Inherited effort hard-fails every Docker Agent spawn.** `base` comes from `effectiveAgentConfig`, which merges the harness-agnostic project `AgentConfig.Effort` and any role override. So `resolved.Effort` is non-empty whenever the project has a default effort (e.g. `high`, set for Claude or Codex), and this check returns `ErrUnsupportedEffort` even though the user never asked for an effort.

The block right below handles this case as "unflagged or inherited effort still clears silently so role/project defaults keep working for every harness". Docker Agent should do the same: fail only when `cfg.EffortOverride && requested.Effort != ""`, and otherwise clear it. The `override=false` test case currently locks in the failing behavior.

**Qualified-version hold only applies to an exact 1.150.0 install.**
- Installed 1.149.0, latest 1.152.0: reports `BehindLatest` → 1.152.0. The user updates, and Chat refuses the new binary.
- Installed 1.151.0: reports current or ahead, with no hint that Chat will refuse it until they downgrade to 1.150.0.

For targets with a qualified version, it would be better to compare against the qualified version instead of the registry's latest.

Rejecting a TUI request returns `ports.ErrChatUnsupported`, but that sentinel means "Chat isn't available for this harness", and clients map it to a "start in terminal" fallback. Here Chat is the *only* supported mode, so `ao spawn --agent docker-agent --mode tui` gets a CHAT_UNSUPPORTED error with the opposite meaning. Any client without TaskComposer's special case may offer a terminal retry that fails again. Consider a distinct error, or a validation error that says terminal mode is unsupported.

`sessionOptions` forwards `settings.Model` as-is, including the catalog placeholder `default` (which `validateTurnSettings` explicitly allows). As far as I can tell, Docker Agent's model config options are the configured model names, so `set_config_option(model, "default")` would likely be rejected and the first turn would fail with `set ACP session option "model"`. The Claude path strips the placeholder; should this one skip sending the option for `default`? (I couldn't confirm this against the native binary.)

`GEMINI_API_KEY` alone makes the `google` provider count as available (so auth shows *configured* and admission passes), but nothing maps it to `GOOGLE_API_KEY` in the launch env. If Docker Agent's Gemini provider reads only `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, the first turn fails at the provider instead of at preflight. Also, the error message in `DefaultConfig` lists `GEMINI_API_KEY` but not `GOOGLE_API_KEY`.

This says "native config required", and the paragraph below says to set `AO_DOCKER_AGENT_CONFIG` before launching. The backend actually generates a default config from `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, or `GOOGLE_API_KEY`/`GEMINI_API_KEY` when it's unset, and `docs/harnesses/docker-agent.md` and `agentauth/plans.go` describe that behavior. **Regression: on some Macs this now fails outright instead of falling back to idle wake.**

`lidSupported` comes from the `lid` capability, which `LidAwake.status()` still reports as available when the helper is in `helper_upgrade_required` or `setup_failed`. With `lidClosed: true`, the daemon's `Start` (`service/awake/service.go`, the `req.LidClosed || nativeGuard` block) returns any `SetupLid()` error. The old idle-only request ignored `ErrLidHelperUpgrade` for exactly this case. `ensureDesktop`'s catch only retries after a safety pause, so the error propagates and no wake is held.

Scenario: a user whose registered helper came from an older AO build (`setup()` deliberately never boots out a registered coordinator, so this is a normal post-upgrade state) clicks the coffee button. Before: idle wake. Now: an error and the Mac can sleep. This contradicts the "idle-only fallback" in the description.

Suggestion: when lid came from the default (not an explicit `setLid(true)`), retry `start(false)` on failure and surface the lid reason as attention. Or exclude `helper_upgrade_required`/`setup_failed` when computing `lidSupported`. The test mock never makes a lid start fail, so a test for this would help.

**Existing mobile ownership is never retired in practice.**

This only runs on the "on" branch, but `on` (line 44) already includes `mobile.keepAwake.enabled`. A user who already has mobile keep-awake persisted sees both controls as on and can't reach this branch without turning off and on again.

- Bridge running: the mobile lease keeps running independently of the configured battery cutoff, which is what the description says this PR prevents.
- Bridge off: both controls show "configured but inactive" attention, and the mobile lease comes back the next time mobile access is turned on.

Suggestion: a one-time migration when status shows the mobile setting persisted (establish desktop wake, then release mobile), or handle it daemon-side.

**Turning lid off can leave only a temporary owner.**

`sessions.some((s) => !s.lidClosed)` counts any non-lid session as the replacement idle owner, including session-scoped and timed ones.

A failed turn-on does not undo what it started. When `before.enabled` was false, `/mobile/enable` has already started the LAN listener on 0.0.0.0 and the cloudflared tunnel. If any later step fails (90 s timeout, tunnel `lastError`, account-token error, `saveAccountRemoteHost` failure), or if there is no connector (`needsConnector`), the bridge stays enabled. Because `on` needs the account record, the switch then shows **off** while this computer is reachable from the internet, and the switch cannot turn it off. `BridgeService.Disable` names this exact state as the one to avoid ("keep the machine reachable from the internet while the UI says it is not"). The tests `gives up with an error when the tunnel never gets an address` and `reports a failed link and stays off` pass but leave `fake.daemon.enabled === true`.

Fix: on failure, return the bridge to its state before this attempt. If `before.enabled` was false, call `POST /api/v1/mobile/disable`. If it was on with `before.noPublicTunnel`, call `POST /api/v1/mobile/enable-lan-only`, which keeps the password and stops the tunnel. For the no-cloudflared branch, either do the same or keep the switch on with a starting state until the install finishes. Add `expect(fake.daemon.enabled).toBe(false)` to the timeout and failed-link tests.

**Launch-time flush sends a sign-out.** `main.ts:2042` sets `{ state: "starting" }` → `invalidate()` flips `pushed=false` while `cloudUserId` is still `null`. On `ready`, `flush()` POSTs `cloudUserId: ""`, and the daemon's `SetCloudUserID("")` sees `telemetry_bound_user=A`, so it retires the install ID and deletes the marker.

Result: every relaunch by a signed-in user rotates the daemon install ID, and daemon events go out under a fresh anon ID until the renderer's ack lands. That's exactly what the `status === "loading"` guard in `TelemetryIdentityRuntime` is trying to prevent. Suggest tracking a `known` flag (set on the first `setCloudUser` call) and having `invalidate()`/`flushOnce()` do nothing until then.

**distinct_id mismatch with desktop.** This uses `p.ExternalID` (the WorkOS `sub`), but the desktop's `session.user.id` comes from `toUserResponse` → `principal.UserID`, which is `ao_users.id` (`auth_store.go` `RETURNING id`). So `invite.sent` lands on a different person than the desktop/daemon/phone events. Should be `p.UserID`; alternatively, switch the desktop to the WorkOS id, but all three surfaces need to use the same one.

**Identifying as the anonymous install ID can block the later merge.** When the desktop isn't signed in, `distinctId` is the `ins_` install ID, and this `identify()` marks that person as identified. If the user then signs in, the desktop `identify(userId)` sends `$anon_distinct_id=ins_…`, and PostHog refuses to merge an already-identified ID. The install's history (and the daemon events on it) never joins the user.

It also creates billed identified profiles for anonymous installs, which contradicts "Anonymous installs stay anonymous" in the rollout note. Suggest only `identify()` when `cloudUserId` is present; otherwise stay anonymous and just `register` the props.

**Opt-out race.** The `analyticsOptedOut` re-check sits before `await loadPostHog()`. If the user toggles off while the chunk loads, `applyAnalyticsOptOut(true)` only sets the flag (`posthogReady` is false). Init then resumes and calls `opt_in_capturing()` unconditionally, so capture runs despite the opt-out. Re-check `analyticsOptedOut` after the await, and call `opt_out_capturing()` instead of opting in when it's set.

A failed turn-on does not undo what it started. When `before.enabled` was false, `/mobile/enable` has already started the LAN listener on 0.0.0.0 and the cloudflared tunnel. If any later step fails (90 s timeout, tunnel `lastError`, account-token error, `saveAccountRemoteHost` failure), or if there is no connector (`needsConnector`), the bridge stays enabled. Because `on` needs the account record, the switch then shows **off** while this computer is reachable from the internet, and the switch cannot turn it off. `BridgeService.Disable` names this exact state as the one to avoid. The tests `gives up with an error when the tunnel never gets an address` and `reports a failed link and stays off` pass but leave `fake.daemon.enabled === true`.

Fix: on failure, return the bridge to its state before this attempt. If `before.enabled` was false, call `POST /api/v1/mobile/disable`. If it was on with `before.noPublicTunnel`, call `POST /api/v1/mobile/enable-lan-only`, which keeps the password and stops the tunnel. For the no-cloudflared branch, either do the same or keep the switch on with a starting state until the install finishes. Add `expect(fake.daemon.enabled).toBe(false)` to the timeout and failed-link tests.

- On with `noPublicTunnel`: `POST /api/v1/mobile/enable-lan-only`, which stops the tunnel and keeps the password.
- On with the tunnel already running: left as it was.

[P2] Keep the model selection isolated until this process reads it

Every launch writes the same Freebuff settings.json before returning argv; the process is started later by Manager.Spawn. Concurrent spawns can interleave A writing GLM, B writing GPT-6 Luna, then A and B both loading GPT-6 Luna. Freebuff 0.2.30 reads these preferences at module initialization ([source](https://github.com/CodebuffAI/freebuff/blob/5be72f534eba560386d22128248878d506a4b01b/cli/src/state/freebuff-model-store.ts#L70)), so atomic rename only prevents torn JSON, and a mutex around the file write alone would still leave the startup race. AO then records/displays A's requested model while A runs a different model. Use a launch-specific preference/config mechanism or otherwise retain isolation through the native settings read.

[P2] Use the session's effective Freebuff config directory for restore

With FREEBUFF_CONFIG_DIR set in project.env, the child receives that override through RuntimeConfig.Env, but restore reads only the daemon environment here. It therefore searches the wrong chats directory and returns ok=false, causing a fresh launch/replay of the saved task instead of continuing the existing conversation. The initial model write has the same mismatch: GetLaunchCommand uses cfg.Env, but Manager.Spawn constructs LaunchConfig without populating Env. Please propagate/resolve the actual session environment across launch and restore so model preferences and chat lookup address the directory the Freebuff process uses.

A bounded native Freebuff 0.2.32 fixture confirmed the launch-side mismatch on original PR commit 1b8a434: the child created its logs under the project's overridden config directory, but AO wrote the requested DeepSeek model into the daemon-level settings file; the project settings contained no freebuffModel. This is not a runtime claim about the displayed model or restore with an override. The fixture was cleaned up and the authenticated demo's prior model settings restored.

[P2] Account for Freebuff's one-time default-model migration

If settings.json lacks the current freebuffModelDefaultMigration stamp, an explicit deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash selection written here is replaced by MiMo on startup. Freebuff 0.2.30 calls migrateSavedDefaultModel when loading the preference; the old default is DeepSeek, and an unstamped old-default value is migrated regardless of whether AO just explicitly selected it ([migration](https://github.com/CodebuffAI/freebuff/blob/5be72f534eba560386d22128248878d506a4b01b/common/src/util/freebuff-default-model-migration.ts#L22), [loader](https://github.com/CodebuffAI/freebuff/blob/5be72f534eba560386d22128248878d506a4b01b/cli/src/utils/settings.ts#L341)). Earlier version/login probes may already stamp a default config, but a fresh project-specific config or a regenerated settings file still triggers this. Preserve the explicit model choice through the migration rather than silently running another model.

A separate local native check also reproduced this with installed Freebuff 0.2.32: starting with only freebuffModel='deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash', launching the binary under a fresh scratch config rewrote it to freebuffModel='mimo/mimo-v2.5' and added the migration stamp. This runtime check is independent of the 0.2.30 source inspection above.

[P2] Match activity markers only in current terminal chrome

The substring search covers every one of the last 12 rows, including transcript and human draft text, and active markers take precedence over the actual idle composer. For example, a completed response containing 'working...' followed by the real 'Enter a coding task' composer is reported as active on every sample. The continuous activity observer persists this false busy state, and coordination delivery suppresses messages while Freebuff is marked active. Parse the current composer/status region instead of treating arbitrary output as authoritative activity; include a regression with a marker in transcript text beside a real idle composer.

[P2] Report unverified credential presence as configured

This returns authorized solely from a nonempty stored token or tokenStore='keychain'; localAuthStatus does the same for any nonempty CODEBUFF_API_KEY. No credential validation or even keychain-secret lookup occurs. A revoked token, arbitrary API key, or orphaned keychain pointer therefore makes the new harness appear ready/signed in even though Freebuff cannot authenticate. The existing ports.AgentAuthStatusConfigured contract explicitly reserves authorized for a successful provider check and uses configured for local credential evidence. Return configured for these local checks (and update the localAuthStatus branch accordingly), or add a bounded verification before claiming authorization.

[P2] Normalize a JSON null settings file before assigning model keys

json.Unmarshal([]byte("null"), &settings) succeeds but replaces the initialized map with nil. The later settings["freebuffModel"] assignment then panics whenever a model is selected, aborting the spawn request instead of returning an error or launching. This is a file Freebuff itself accepts as empty settings ([validateSettings](https://github.com/CodebuffAI/freebuff/blob/5be72f534eba560386d22128248878d506a4b01b/cli/src/utils/settings.ts#L146)). Reinitialize a nil map after decoding, or reject the non-object shape with a normal error, and cover this case.

Addressed in c688f76 with two parts.
1. **Priming Enter.** `ports.AgentAfterStartSubmitConfirmer` asks AO to send a lone Enter into the empty, ready composer before typing. Freebuff ignores an empty submit, and on Linux it treats `\n` as Enter until it has seen a Return.
2. **Confirmation.** After typing, the manager reads the rendered screen until the adapter reports the turn submitted: running chrome or an empty composer. At a8d8e7b, creating an AO profile while the source native OAuth lock is held copies `auth/prod/en/mcode-public/auth.lock.lock` into the new private profile. After the real source owner exits, that copied directory has no owner but the actual native OAuth initializer waits on it: bounded-timeout after 1501 ms, versus completion in 4 ms after removing only the copied lock. Native default staleMs=30000 is source-validated; this is a measured initialization stall, not a permanent-failure or frequency claim. Filter native synchronization directories rather than importing them as credential state. The review body includes the real native-owner/production-GetAgentHooks reproduction and remove-only control.

This new command-backed catalog reads the native profile/config, but MiniMax has no config/default/provider fingerprint source, so CatalogFingerprint returns executable metadata only. At a8d8e7b, real native provider-list returned A then B after editing one config.yaml, while both fingerprints were aa8a41a3bc993c5c. The production Service reported changed-input=false and kept removed A in the cache-first picker; an explicit refresh returned B. [P2] Preserve visible text between OSC sequences

The OSC branch's `[^\x07]*` is greedy and includes `ESC \\`, so ST-terminated OSC8 hyperlinks match through the closing hyperlink sequence and consume their visible label. Reproduced: `before <OSC8-open>IMPORTANT<OSC8-close> after` sanitizes to `before  after`; multiple hyperlinks can also swallow intervening output. Stop at the first BEL/ST terminator and add a regression case with an ST-terminated OSC8 hyperlink.

[P2] Cap the streamed text keys emitted by the daemon

The conversation controller emits MCP progress as `detail.progress` and file-change prose as `detail.patchOutput` (`streamedTextKeys` in `controllers/conversations.go`), but neither key is in this whitelist. With the default `--cap 1000`, JSON output preserves a 32,768-character value in either field and records zero truncations, defeating the advertised per-field bound. Include both wire keys and cover them with truncation tests.

[P2] Cap scalar strings inside nested tool arrays

This branch sends each nested array element back into `walkCap`, but a scalar string immediately returns because the function only accepts maps or arrays at entry. An MCP argument/result containing `{"values":[["<10,000-character cell>"]]}` therefore retains the entire cell under `--cap 1000`, with no truncation record; flat string arrays are handled by the other branch. Handle and replace string elements at every array depth, and test a two-dimensional tool payload.

[P2] Keep small caps within budget without discarding all content

When the recovery marker is longer than a valid cap, returning it whole exceeds the limit and retains neither the original head nor tail. Reproduced with a 1,000-character field, session `demo-1`, sequence 2, and `--cap 80`: the result is a 96-character marker claiming 920 characters were omitted, although all 1,000 original characters are gone. Use a compact marker when the command cannot fit, retain source text within the budget, and calculate the omitted count from the text actually kept.

[P2] Preserve API error diagnostics when the session mode changes

If the session switches from Chat to TUI after `fetchScopedSession` but before the conversation GET, the daemon returns `SESSION_MODE_MISMATCH`. Replacing `apiResponseError` with `transcriptUnavailable` removes the code and request ID, preventing error classification and log correlation and violating the repository's error-envelope rule. Preserve or wrap the original error when adding Terminal UI guidance. If `CHAT_INTERFACE_TRANSITION` is received, it should also retain its retry-after-handoff guidance rather than being described as permanent Terminal UI mode/no durable transcript.

[P2] Persist MiniMax's accepted native Ask choice before shipping Chat

In an Auto session, selecting the advertised native Ask option (`permissionMode=default`, category `_permission`) succeeds but leaves AO's saved approval policy at `auto`. The connected `permissionConfigOptions` code only recognizes ID `mode` and has no MiniMax mapping, so `settingsFromConfigOptions` never updates approval. The next dispatch still carries `Approval=auto`, which `minimaxacp.sessionOptions` translates back to `permissionMode=auto`, undoing the user's stricter choice. The self-contained proof uses a provider double with actual captured native metadata; it proves service/dispatch state, not subsequent native tool execution or Electron behavior. No bypass value is used, so this is independent of the enum-spelling finding.

[P1] Honor explicit settings when the picked target is already active

Swallowing `ErrProviderAlreadyActive` also accepts a fresh message whose requested settings differ from the active target. Reproduced through the production HTTP controller and real SQLite: client A switches to Claude with `bypass-permissions`/`model-old`; client B, still showing the old source, sends a new `clientMessageId` selecting Claude with `accept-edits`/`model-picked`. B gets HTTP 200 and `duplicate:false`, but the delivered turn has `Approval:bypass-permissions` and `Model:model-old`. Only matching retries can safely reuse the active target; validate/apply the explicit settings or refuse before sending. [Complete runnable test and output](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6588#issuecomment-6309746825) (B1).

[P2] Bind attachment sends to the selected switch target

The attachment path still releases the switch lock before its message is sent, so the text-path atomic fix does not cover images. The production HTTP reproduction switches to Claude (200), lets another client switch to OpenCode (200), then sends a valid 1x1 PNG (202): Claude receives nothing and OpenCode receives both the image and "Only Claude should inspect this image". Use an atomic attachment send or bind the later send to the selected controller generation. [Runnable test and captured routing](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6588#issuecomment-6309746825) (B2).

[P2] Fence stale turns before recording terminal responses

The recorder now follows the native-thread fence but still precedes turn/timestamp correlation. With the same launch and native thread, replay turn-1's Stop after turn-2's prompt: real SQLite persists `SECOND REQUEST -> FIRST ANSWER`; the actual second answer cannot replace it because the newest terminal row is already closed. The lifecycle checkpoint can reject the stale event while the independent history write has already corrupted handoff context. Carry/check turn identity and freshness before closing the terminal row. [Deterministic SQLite reproduction](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6588#issuecomment-6309746825) (B3).

[P2] Reset unknown Plan state after a cold native resume too

`planUnknown` is set only for a surviving-host reconnect. On cold `thread/resume`, it remains false, so the first turn with the UI's `Plan:false` omits `collaborationMode` and Codex keeps the persisted Plan mode. The adapter test reproduces that omission; a separate real Codex 0.162.1 run records modes `plan -> process restart -> plan` without an override, while an explicit `default` control resets it. Mark cold-resumed collaboration state unknown as well. [Test, live script and captured mode sequence](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6588#issuecomment-6309746825) (B4).

[P2] Restore source ownership and launch options in one transaction

Rollback still commits `sourceLaunch` separately before restoring source ownership. A fault injected immediately after the real SQLite options commit leaves the durable owner as Codex, its native ID empty, and its target handoff erased by Claude's options; explicit Resume consequently has neither the source identity nor the target context. This differs from a switch merely remaining stopped until Resume. Use the same atomic owner/options operation on rollback and handle its error. [SQLite crash-cut reproduction](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6588#issuecomment-6309746825) (B5).

[P2] Retain handoff context until native history can be resumed

`confirmTUISwitchTargetAlive` proves only that a child survives 1.5s, so this clears the note even while `AgentSessionID` is empty. If the first native hook is delayed/missed and the child then exits, ordinary Restore starts fresh with the session's original task instead of the switch context. The deterministic manager/runtime-double reproduction successfully launches the handoff, then restores to `ORIGINAL TASK ALREADY COMPLETED`; Muse's real restore helper explicitly takes this fresh path when no native ID has been emitted. Keep or reconstruct the note until resumable native history is established. [Complete conditional reproduction](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6588#issuecomment-6309746825) (B6).

[P2] Read favorite options from the new model catalog

These callbacks capture the outgoing model's `acpEffortOption`/`fastOption` and discard the replacement catalog returned by the model mutation. Four rendered-component regressions reproduce missing effort/Fast writes when the target newly offers them, an obsolete Fast value after its choices change, and a stale PATCH when the target removes Fast. The same-model Fast tests pass because they never change the option catalog. Resolve dependent options from each completed mutation's target catalog before applying the saved setup. [Complete patch, commands and failing output](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6588#issuecomment-6309621284) (F1).

[P2] Apply saved Thinking when restoring Cursor favorites

The new favorite handler never reads `setup.thinking`, although Cursor's Thinking choice is saved in the setup and exposed as a select-form on/off control. Both saved On and saved Off reproduce only model and effort writes, leaving the current Thinking value unchanged. Apply the saved Thinking choice through the live target option as part of restoring the favorite. [Both runnable assertion failures](https://github.com/OrchestratorInc/agent-orchestrator/pull/6588#issuecomment-6309621284) (F2).

[P2] Verify current source cleanliness before accepting the fallback

At `f11f91e`, a clean-looking `vgit.<sha>` banner does not establish a clean working tree: native [trusts a same-commit source stamp and its stored dirty flag](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/d923a5eb487a17c0a68801bba9ef0f56c81040a8/hermes_cli/version_info.py#L166-L201). Reproduced with the actual released `d923a5e` source and actual native `write_source_stamp`, without hand-written stamp JSON:

1. In a clean tagless checkout, produce the native stamp (`dirty:false`, `displayVersion:git.d923a5e`), import the real annotated `v0.22.2` ref, and pack refs; the clean control passes.
2. Change only tracked `locales/en.yaml` so `cli.tui.placeholder_busy` is `REVIEW LOCAL BUSY`.
3. Git reports `M locales/en.yaml`, and native i18n returns that changed busy text, while a fresh native version process still prints `Hermes Agent vgit.d923a5e (2026.9.24) · upstream d923a5eb`.

Expected: decline this fallback because the current source differs from the qualified release. Observed: `SourceReleaseTag="v0.22.2"` and a fresh `probeNativeVersion=true`, so AO admits modified composer chrome as qualified. Check current tracked-source cleanliness independently before accepting the fallback. This is the new source fallback's stated prerequisite; it does not claim every pre-existing semver path detected local edits. Executed source helpers and fresh AO gate on macOS, without a TUI/provider turn.

[P2] Resolve annotated tag objects stored in packs

At `f11f91e`, a loose tag ref can point to a packed object; opening only `.git/objects/<prefix>/<suffix>` does not cover that normal Git state. On the actual clean `d923a5e` source, retain the actual native-generated `git.d923a5e` stamp and real upstream annotated `v0.22.2` tag, then run:

```sh
tag=$(git rev-parse refs/tags/v0.22.2)
git repack -a -d
git update-ref -d refs/tags/v0.22.2
git update-ref refs/tags/v0.22.2 "$tag"
```

`git status --porcelain` is empty; `git tag --points-at HEAD` returns `v0.22.2`; `git cat-file -t 7b77e29eedd85a8497ce2821448dac7964dc46f6` returns `tag`. Expected: accept the same clean qualified checkout as the packed-ref control. Observed: `releaseTagsAt=[]`, `SourceReleaseTag=""`, and a fresh version probe rejects the actual native banner. Resolve annotated tags through the full object database, including packs/alternates, so storage layout does not disable an installed qualified agent. The native stamp/banner comes from [the released producer](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/d923a5eb487a17c0a68801bba9ef0f56c81040a8/hermes_cli/source_stamp.py) and [reader](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/d923a5eb487a17c0a68801bba9ef0f56c81040a8/hermes_cli/version_info.py#L129-L203); this is an executed source/gate probe, not a full installer or Windows run.

[P2] Honor loose refs before accepting a packed release tag

At `f11f91e`, the packed scan adds a tag even when a newer loose ref of the same name shadows it. Minimal real-Git fixture (two commits `A` then `B`): tag `v0.22.2` at `A`, `git pack-refs --all`, advance to `B`, `git tag -f v0.22.2 B`, then detach at `A`. This is reachable after a manual retag/forced tag fetch; the ordinary native updater need not retag.

Expected: reject `A` through this fallback because the effective release tag is at `B`. Observed: `git rev-parse v0.22.2^{}` returns `B`, both `git tag --points-at HEAD` and `git tag --merged HEAD --list 'v[0-9]*'` are empty, and actual pinned [native version derivation](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/d923a5eb487a17c0a68801bba9ef0f56c81040a8/hermes_cli/version_info.py#L239-L265) plus its banner formatter emits `Hermes Agent vgit.66e89a6 …` for `A`; nevertheless `SourceReleaseTag="v0.22.2"` and a fresh AO version gate returns `true` from the stale packed `A` entry. Restoring the loose tag to `A` is the accepted positive control. [Git uses packed refs only when the loose ref is absent](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-pack-refs/2.56.0); discard shadowed packed entries before qualifying a release.

This fallback timer is never cleared when the WebView it belongs to goes away. Scenario: an inline page fires `onLoadEnd` (timer armed for ~2s), then the user scrolls it out of range before the bridge reports a height. `live` turns false, the WebView unmounts and `unload()` sets `loading` back to true, but the timer still fires and calls `ready()`. When the frame comes back into range, the new WebView mounts with `loading === false`, so there is no skeleton while it loads and the frame resizes on screen when the height arrives. That is the jump this PR is trying to prevent. `page.gone()` (a process restart) has the same problem: a timer armed by the dead page marks the remounted one ready early.

Fix: clear `readyFallback.current` whenever the mounted document goes away, for example in the `!live` effect next to `unload()` and when `page.mount` changes. Or key the timer to the mount it was armed for and ignore it if the mount has changed.

Fixed in 2a19af4e01. The fallback timer now belongs to the page that armed it: it's cleared when the frame leaves range and whenever the page remounts (`page.mount` changes, which covers the process-death path).

It also covers the fallback for a page that never reports a height, and the normal path where the page reports its height.

If a session claims PR X successfully, then later re-claims X and fails (PR merged/closed -> `ErrPRNotOpen`, a transient SCM fetch error, review enrichment error), the original "Claimed a pull request" row flips to Failed with the new error. That overwrites a confirmed success. Failures should get their own ID, e.g. `failureOperationID(ctx, "claim")` like the other actions, or a fresh uuid like rename.

**P2:** this filters on `provider_item_id` alone, but the only index is `(conversation_id, provider_item_id)`, so SQLite can't use it. `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` on a real DB gives `SCAN conversation_activities`. It runs synchronously on every `Kill`/`RequestKill` (via `spawnParent`), including once per session in `TeardownProject`'s parallel loop. Cost grows with total chat history. Add an index on `provider_item_id`, or persist the parent on the child session instead of searching activities for it.

**P2:** `RequestKill` only acknowledges terminal intent ("without waiting for cleanup scripts"), but this records the terminate action as Completed. Cleanup can still fail afterwards and the row will keep saying Completed. Either label it as requested/running here and settle on cleanup, or record only from the path that confirms termination.

**P2:** this puts the raw error code (e.g. `TARGET_START_FAILED`) into the activity's `error`, which the expanded row shows to the user as-is. Map it to a readable message, or carry the switch's stored error message if there is one.

**P2:** `SwitchAgent` deliberately skips validation/admission rejections ("Validation rejections are not actions"), but `ClaimPR` records `requireProjectPRRepository` rejections and the SCM-unavailable case (line 102) as failed actions. Pick one rule so the chat doesn't fill with rows for requests that never started.
**Nit:** `key={line}` can repeat (an error message equal to a name, or the same harness on both sides), which causes React duplicate-key warnings. Use the index; the list is static.

**P2: no feedback for up to ~20 s on a slow failure.** "Connecting…" only appears after the first race fails, because `onWaiting` runs before each retry. When the code has a tunnel endpoint that can't be reached, `probeEndpoint` keeps retrying it every 2 s for `TUNNEL_PROBE_WINDOW_MS` (20 s). The first race therefore takes about 20 s, and the user gets the scan haptic and then nothing. The scanner also ignores the code during that time, so it looks frozen.

Repro on device: pair once so access is confirmed, turn on Airplane Mode, then scan a code that has a tunnel. The haptic fires, nothing is shown for about 20 s, then the error appears. The same happens whenever the tunnel is down, so it isn't just an offline edge case. It also means "later unreachable scans show the error immediately" doesn't hold for codes with a tunnel.

Suggested fix: show the connecting state as soon as `pair()` starts (e.g. render it off `busy` too), and keep the Local Network line for when `awaitingLocalNetwork` is set. Separately, `shouldRetryProbe` could skip the tunnel retry when the failure is the instant "offline" error rather than DNS, but that's outside this PR.

[P2] Sanitize import failures before returning their text

This turns every unclassified pending-import error into a public API message. Errors from prepareImportedWorkspace include raw filesystem errors and importGit's stderr, and those paths return before resumeChatController's RedactError call. For example, a failing source Git lookup now sends its local paths and raw diagnostic text to the client, whereas the normal toAPIError/envelope path would return a generic internal error. Keep the useful import failure code, but expose only an explicitly safe, bounded diagnostic and redact configured values before building the API error.

[P2] Refresh the diff base when a copy retry advances HEAD

The diff base is computed only inside `if created`, but the workspace is persisted before copying and copyImportedWorkspace resets an existing workspace to the source's current HEAD on every retry. If the first copy fails, the source commits again, and the user retries, the workspace moves to the new commit while DiffBaseSHA/Ref still describe the first attempt. The Files view then includes intervening source commits as changes made by this session. Recompute and persist the base for the commit actually transferred, including the existing-workspace retry path.

[P2] Treat children of a replaced directory as deleted

On Unix, a valid dirty checkout can replace a tracked directory with an ordinary file: HEAD contains `dir/child`, while the working tree contains the untracked file `dir`. importChanges then includes both `dir` and the deleted `dir/child`, but Lstat(`dir/child`) returns ENOTDIR, which does not match os.ErrNotExist. This returns an error before the deletion-first copy logic can run, so opening this conversation fails on every retry. Recognize a non-directory ancestor as a missing child (without swallowing unrelated I/O errors), and cover this directory-to-file transition.

[P2] Deduplicate Codex representations per message instead of globally

`pick` selects a representation for the entire combined history. A thread whose earlier segment has response-only user messages and whose later segment has event-user messages loses every earlier prompt as soon as one event-user record is present; similarly, one response-assistant causes event-only answers elsewhere to disappear. This can happen when a conversation is continued through different Codex clients or versions, and the parser already accepts all of these formats. The imported archive and title silently omit legitimate history without the shortened indicator. Match duplicate representations for the same message/turn while retaining messages that have no preferred-format counterpart.

Including the real .gitconfig by absolute path preserves its direct values, but Git still expands any include.path beginning with ~/ against the process HOME, not the directory containing that config. [P2] Give discovery its own timeout after the readiness wait
