**[P2] Retain the temporary URI permission owner through the asynchronous read**

The queued job captures only `uris` and `resolver`, so the accepted `ContentInfoCompat` payload and its underlying `InputContentInfo` can become unreachable as soon as this callback returns. Android ties the temporary IME read permission to that object: garbage collection can release it before a queued worker opens the stream. A valid image inserted from Gboard can then fail with a permission error and be reported as unreadable, especially when the single reader is busy with another image.

Please retain the accepted payload, including its permission owner, until all asynchronous image reads finish. [Android's permission-lifetime contract](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/view/inputmethod/InputContentInfo#requestPermission()) and [AndroidX's implementation](https://github.com/androidx/androidx/blob/androidx-main/core/core/src/main/java/androidx/core/view/inputmethod/InputConnectionCompat.java) describe this lifetime requirement. This finding is based on code inspection; I have not reproduced it on a device.

**[P2] Bound the native paste batch before reading and encoding discarded images**

This loop reads every clipboard image into `items`, then the background job builds the full base64 batch while the source array remains retained. The composer's 8-item / 25 MB limits only run after the entire native event reaches JavaScript. Copying a large selection of photos can therefore allocate hundreds of MB for images that will ultimately be discarded, creating memory pressure and an app-termination risk. The 10 MB per-image check does not bound the complete batch. Android's `emit()` similarly accumulates every encoded image before applying the JS limits.

Please enforce native item-count and cumulative-byte budgets before retaining or encoding excess items, report the overflow, and keep the JS gate for the existing attachment-store budget. This is a code-derived allocation issue; no device crash was reproduced during this review.

Good catch. Fixed in 26c8482247.

The background job now captures the original `payload` (the accepted `ContentInfoCompat`), not just its URIs. It reads the images and then, in a `finally`, calls `releaseImeGrant(payload)`. That looks up the `InputContentInfo` that AndroidX's `InputConnectionCompat` stores in the extras (`androidx.core.view.extra.INPUT_CONTENT_INFO`, after its `requestPermission()`) and calls `releasePermission()` on it, on API 25+. Because the payload is used after the last read, it, and the `InputContentInfo` that owns the grant, stays strongly reachable while the queued reads run. And the grant is returned promptly once they finish instead of waiting for GC.

[P2] Start a fresh poll after network recovery

If a board request is still hanging when the phone goes offline and comes back online, and the endpoint race selects the same URL, reloadConfig preserves the config object and fetchAll() joins the existing primaryLoadRef promise rather than starting a fresh request. Recovery therefore waits for the old request to time out and then the next polling interval, despite a verified working endpoint. I reproduced this with a deferred board request: the network-return callback completed its race but started zero new board requests. Cancel the stale in-flight load before starting the recovery poll.

[P2] Let an explicit incompatibility error override reconnecting

After an unanswered poll sets linkHealth to reconnecting, a subsequent endpoint race can throw IncompatibleHostVersionError. reloadConfig then sets errorStatus to 426 and clears the config without updating the link tracker, so this unconditional branch continues showing Reconnecting / This usually clears on its own instead of the upgrade guidance. No session poll can clear the tracker while the config is null, and repeated incompatible races leave it unchanged. A store-level reproduction confirms errorStatus === 426 with linkHealth still reconnecting. Record an answered-error in that catch path, or give explicit answered errors precedence here and in StaleBanner.

**A registration that fails is never announced, so a slow or dropped first request loses the wake.** `onViewing` fires only for the `send(next, next)` registration; renewals pass `announce = false`. Suppose that first POST rejects: the 12 s `apiRequest` timeout during a slow provider start, a mobile network blip, or a 5xx. The renewal 15 s later is then what actually registers and wakes the chat, but nothing re-reads the conversation. The snapshot stays `hibernated`, `providerLive` never flips, and the composer is back to "Ask when unsure" until the chat is reopened. That is the bug this PR fixes.

Track whether this lease has been announced. Fire `onViewing` on the first *successful* `active: true` POST, registration or renewal, and reset the flag when the lease is released for background. Older daemons stay quiet in the "does not report a registration the daemon rejected" case, because every renewal fails there too. Please add a test where the first registration rejects, a renewal succeeds, and `onViewing` is called once.

**The reload-on-wake decision has no test.** This effect is what fixes the bug in the PR title: when the provider goes from not live to `ready`/`busy`, it reloads the catalog and skips the cache. - first snapshot already live: plain load
- hibernated to ready: refresh
- busy to recovering to ready: refresh again
- repeat render with the same state: no request

Move the decision into a small pure helper next to `providerCatalogLive` in `turnOptionsCatalog.ts`. The temp name is always `${filePath}.part`, which can collide:
- The Download menu item stays clickable while a save runs, so two downloads to the same path write the same `.part` concurrently and the interleaved result is renamed into place.
- If the folder already has an unrelated `report.pdf.part`, it's overwritten, and on failure `rm(partial, { force: true })` deletes it.

A unique sibling avoids both, e.g. `${filePath}.${randomUUID()}.part` opened with `flags: "wx"`. It stays in the same directory, so the rename is still atomic.

The dialog now opens before the request, so an expired access link (401/403) or a deleted file (404) surfaces only after the user has chosen where to save. Before, the fetch failed first.

Could the handler `session.fetch` and check `response.ok` first, then show the dialog, then pipe the body? On cancel, call `response.body?.cancel()`. The body isn't read while the dialog is open, so backpressure keeps memory flat, and "refuses before any dialog" also holds for bad responses, not just malformed links.

Now that large files work, this await can run for a minute or more (200 MiB took 60 s in the PR's test), and the UI shows nothing: no pending state, no completion message, and Download can be clicked again, which leads to the `.part` collision above.

At minimum, disable the item or show a spinner while it's pending, and show a short success message when it resolves `true`. Byte progress could be a follow-up.

Nit: browsers ignore the `download` attribute for cross-origin URLs, so in the plain browser preview this opens or navigates to the artifact instead of saving it. Fine for a dev fallback; maybe say so in a comment so nobody relies on it.

With unlimited sizes, a download can run for many minutes, and nothing here bounds or stops it:
- **No timeout.** If the connection stalls, `pipeline` waits forever, and the IPC call (and the UI) never settles. An idle timeout (abort when no bytes arrive for N seconds) would turn a stall into a clear error.
- **No cancel.** Once started, a multi-GB download can't be stopped. Passing an `AbortSignal` into `session.fetch` and `pipeline`, with a way for the renderer to trigger it, would cover both cases.
- **Link expiry.** The artifact link comes from a short-lived access prefix. Is the signature checked only when the request starts? If the control plane can cut an in-flight response when the link expires, long downloads will fail partway. That would need a fresh link plus `Range` resume, or at least a clear error.

The `catch` removes the `.part` when the stream errors, but not when the app quits or crashes mid-download. With large files, that can leave gigabytes of `.part` files in the user's folder. Worth tracking in-flight partial paths and removing them on `before-quit`. A unique temp name (see the earlier comment on line 58) also makes stale ones easy to recognise.

**Cloud HTML failure states render unreadable and can't be clicked.** `CloudArtifactFrame` shows its own `PanelMessage` states: loading, `artifacts.unavailable` on 404, and `artifacts.accessError` with a Retry button. Here they render inside the 1000px box scaled to card width (about 0.25×), so the `text-xs` label comes out around 3px. The thumbnail root is `inert` and `pointer-events-none`, so Retry can't be clicked. Local HTML shows the Globe "No preview available" placeholder in the same cases.

Suggestion: do the HEAD check here, like the local `pageAvailable` path, but through `cloudCpFetch`. Fall back to the icon on a 404 or other error, and mount the frame only after a 2xx. A fallback/`onUnavailable` prop on `CloudArtifactFrame` would also work.

**Each cloud SVG is downloaded twice.** `fetchSessionArtifactFile` only sends HEAD for media kinds or for paths that don't match `CLOUD_TEXT_ARTIFACT`. `.svg` is not a media kind and does match `CLOUD_TEXT_ARTIFACT`, so this availability check GETs the whole SVG body over the bridge, and then the `` fetches it again. The new test asserts HEAD for `cover.png` but checks nothing for `logo.svg`, so it doesn't catch this. Please use HEAD here when the read is only an availability check.

**Refused reads trigger one token request per card.** `refetch()` defaults to `cancelRefetch: true`. When the link expires, every visible thumbnail in the session gets a 403 and calls this, so K access requests reach the control plane. All but the last are aborted on the client, but only after they were sent. Also, if the control plane keeps minting tokens while the file route keeps refusing, the cycle "new token → 403 → refetch" never stops. Consider `access.refetch({ cancelRefetch: false })`, plus a guard so a given file URL triggers at most one refresh.

**Some cloud cards can stay blank.** If the access query is disabled (`ready` is false or `orgId` is empty), it never runs. `data` stays undefined and `isError` stays false, so this stays true and the card renders nothing forever. Before this PR it showed the placeholder icon. Separately, line 33 requests access for every visible non-HTML cloud row, including types that can't be previewed (PDF, `.jsonl`, archives). Those cards stay blank until the token arrives, then show the icon anyway. Suggestion: treat access as pending only while it is actually fetching (`access.fetchStatus !== "idle"`), and enable access only when the row has a cloud-previewable type.

[P2] Finish the attribution step only after persistence succeeds

The cache is changed to the selected answer (and a skip is reported) before `recordAcquisitionChannel` succeeds. If the IPC rejects because the marker cannot be written, `.catch(() => false)` silently leaves that optimistic value cached with `staleTime: Infinity`: the card disappears, the completion/skip phase is permanently reserved, and the answer is lost while the on-disk state remains pending. The question then returns on the next launch, potentially with an already-recorded, contradictory terminal phase. Wait for successful persistence before hiding/reporting the terminal phase, or roll back and allow retry on failure; distinguish a failed write from an answer already recorded elsewhere. Add a rejected-IPC test that verifies the question remains retryable and no completed/skipped phase is recorded.

[P2] Include archived projects in the upgrade guard

`firstProject` comes from `len(ListProjects(...)) == 0`, but that query excludes archived rows, and `Remove` archives projects rather than deleting them. An existing install that removed its projects before upgrading therefore claims the new marker and exports `first_for_install: true` on its next add, despite its prior project rows still being available. Use `CountProjectsIncludingArchived` before the add for the durable flag (keeping the legacy event's active-project behavior separate), and cover an upgrade with only archived projects.

[P2] Coordinate the first-session check with milestone ownership

The prior-session check runs before `manager.Spawn`, while the marker is claimed only after it returns. Spawn persists a seed row before doing workspace/runtime provisioning, so A can observe an empty install and remain provisioning while B sees A's row, completes first, and claims the marker with `firstSession=false`. When A finishes, its claim also returns false: neither successful spawn ever exports `first_for_install: true`, and the marker makes that loss permanent. Coordinate marker ownership with the initial eligibility check so a later ineligible spawn cannot consume the eligible spawn's claim; add a concurrent test that holds A after row creation while B finishes.

[P2] Scope asynchronous completions to the pending launch

`recheck` settles or updates whichever request is currently in the global store, without checking that it is still the request that started this operation. For example, start an install/check for project A, dismiss its dialog, then open a blocked launch for project B: when A completes, this code can resolve B using A's harness and readiness result, causing B to spawn without its blockers being cleared. A still-blocked result can instead replace B's report/input with A's. Give pending launches a stable identity and ignore completions after cancellation or replacement, including the install and login continuations. Add coverage with a deferred completion from A after B opens.

[P2] Clear agent-specific effort when switching worker harnesses

The preflight outcome can change `agent`, and the model is correctly discarded in that case, but `input.effort` still comes from the original agent. A Codex task with an explicit effort such as `high` that switches to an installed opencode/Gemini agent passes preflight and then fails with `UNSUPPORTED_EFFORT`: delegation marks request-carried effort as `EffortOverride`, and `resolveAgentConfig` rejects it for those harnesses. Only carry effort over when the agent is unchanged, or resolve valid tuning for the newly selected agent. Cover the switch with a nonempty original effort.

[P2] Preserve the repository behind a default-branch blocker

For a workspace child with an empty stored `DefaultBranch` and no resolvable remote HEAD, this returns the same undifferentiated blocker as a failure in the root repository. The dialog's only branch fix calls `setProjectDefaultBranch`, which updates the root project config; the next check still uses the child's unchanged `repo.DefaultBranch` and stays blocked. Repeatedly saving the correct child branch therefore never lets the user continue, and the dialog does not identify which child needs repair. Return the affected repository and provide a fix that applies to that repository, with coverage for a resolved root and unresolved child.

This grid relies on `flexWrap` in a box sized to exactly 4 dots + 3 gaps. That breaks on some Android densities.

Yoga lays out in 32-bit floats. It starts a new line when the running sum is strictly greater than the available width, with no tolerance. So whether the 4th dot fits depends on how `DOT`, `GAP` and `SIZE` each round to float32.

At PixelRatio 2.625 (420 dpi, the standard `DENSITY_420` bucket):
- `DOT` = 7/2.625 and `GAP` = 3/2.625 = 8/7 both round **up** to float32.
- `SIZE` = 296/21 rounds **down**.
- In units of 2^-20, the exact sum 4*DOT_f + 3*GAP_f is 14779928.875 and Yoga running sum ends at 14779930, against SIZE_f = 14779928.

So the 4th dot of each row wraps. The lattice becomes 3 columns by 6 rows spilling out of its box, and the trail no longer runs round the edge. At iOS 3x it fits only because both sides land on exactly 14330539, which is why the simulator looked right. Users can also change Display size on Android, which produces other fractional densities.

Please lay the dots out without wrap math. Either render four row `View`s (`flexDirection: "row", gap: GAP`) inside a column with `gap: GAP`, or position each dot absolutely at `col * (DOT + GAP), row * (DOT + GAP)`. That way no density can reflow the lattice.

**High: one standalone session stalls all usage export.** Standalone workers (`ao spawn --standalone`) have `sessions.project_id = NULL`, but their human Chat messages are still counted. Here `s.project_id` is scanned into `b.ProjectID string`, so the whole drain fails with:

```
drain usage messages: sql: Scan error on column index 1, name "project_id": converting NULL to string is unsupported
```

`flush` returns on that error before `flushPRs`, so **no** `messages_sent` or `worker_pr_*` event leaves the install from then on. The bad row can't drain because only a successful drain resets it.

Reproduced by hand in an isolated daemon (lab `AO_DATA_DIR`, fake PostHog on loopback):
1. `ao spawn --standalone --mode chat ...` gives `usage_message_summary` = `standalone-1|1` (project NULL).
2. A project session `lab-3` gets 1 pending message, and one PR is marked pending.
3. `POST /internal/telemetry/usage-flush` returns 204, the WARN above is logged, 0 events are sent, and `lab-3` and the PR stay pending.
4. Control: after zeroing the standalone row, the same flush sends both `messages_sent` and `worker_pr_associated`.

Suggest either not incrementing for sessions without a project (in `appendUserMessage` or the query) or adding `AND s.project_id IS NOT NULL` here. Also, one bad row shouldn't block the rest of the batch. A regression test with a standalone session would catch this.

**High for opted-out installs: this UPDATE is quadratic and runs every minute under the write lock.** It has no `WHERE` and rewrites every `usage_pr_measurement` row. The correlated `EXISTS` matches on a computed `CASE` key that can't use the `pr` index, so each row scans `pr` in full.

Timed with the sqlite3 CLI on a copy of a migrated lab DB:

| PR rows | time |
|---|---|
| 5,000 | 4.1 s |
| 10,000 | 17.0 s |

By contrast, `PendingWorkerPRUsage` is fine at 9 ms, because the planner scans `pr` once and probes `m` by primary key.

This UPDATE runs through `flush()` whenever the install is opted out:
- on the 1-minute ticker
- synchronously in `startUsageTelemetry` before the HTTP server is up, which delays daemon start
- on every session Kill/RequestKill, via `usageArchiveFlush`

All of these hold `s.writeMu`, so other store writes queue behind it. The privacy-conscious users are the ones who pay for it.

Suggestions: only touch rows that are still pending (`WHERE associated_reported = 0 OR merged_reported = 0`). Match on indexable columns, e.g. store `pr_url` (or provider/host/provider_id) in the measurement table instead of the concatenated key. Run the discard once on the opt-out transition rather than every minute.

**Medium: worker opening prompts are counted as direct human messages even when an orchestrator or automation spawned the worker.** `StartChatTurn` (`service/chat/service.go`) and `QueueChatPrompt` (`daemon/lifecycle_wiring.go`) hard-code `Origin: MessageOriginHuman` with no `SenderSessionID` for every spawn. So this condition counts them no matter who called `ao spawn`: an orchestrator agent (`AO_SESSION_ID` set) or the automation scheduler.

Verified by hand: a plain `ao spawn --mode chat --prompt ...` sets `pending_count = 1` before anyone has typed in Chat. An orchestrator spawning 20 workers will add 20 "direct human Chat messages". The PR description says worker automation is excluded, but this is automation-authored.

The data to tell them apart already exists: `SpawnConfig.ParentSessionID`, `SpawnConfig.AutomationRunID` and `sessions.automation_run_id`. It just doesn't reach the chat launcher.

Results from the other paths I tested by hand:

- Re-sending the same `clientMessageId` doesn't double-count.

**Major — daemon Sentry is now permanently off on Windows, and the PR/docs don't say so.**

On win32 the desktop authority never writes the policy file (`durabilitySupported = false`, `load()` returns early in `telemetry-policy-file.ts`). Before this change, missing file + the packaged `AO_TELEMETRY_EVENTS=on` meant `!snapshot.Present` → allowed, so Windows daemon 5xx/panics reached Sentry. Now `snapshot.Present` is required, so they never do. Even a hand-written valid file can't help: `Read` rejects `Perm()&0o077 != 0`, and Go reports `0666` for regular files on Windows.

Reproduced locally on Windows against the real `Reader` + `sentryobs` with a fake ingest: base → `EventsAllowed=true`, 1 event; this PR → `false`, 0 events.

Fail-closed may well be the right privacy outcome given Windows has no consent UI, but the PR's "Known platform limit" only mentions Electron. Please either call out that daemon error reporting also stops on Windows (PR body + `docs/telemetry.md` Sentry section), or decide that Windows needs a different rule. Worth confirming with whoever owns the #7386 coverage work, since that just landed.

**Question — new installs get error sharing on with no prompt.** Flipping this also changes what a *fresh* packaged macOS/Linux install does: `TelemetryPolicyAuthority.load()` materializes `newRecord(packagedDefault=true)` with `consent_production_enabled: true`, `replace()` marks it acknowledged, `consentRenewalRequired` is false, so no dialog shows, and both Electron Sentry and (via `reader.go`) daemon Sentry start immediately.

Meanwhile existing users, whose v1/v2 `events_enabled: true` mostly came from that same packaged default rather than an explicit choice, get the "Turn on" renewal dialog. So upgrades must opt in and new installs are opted in silently. The PR's "Both daemon and Electron Sentry remain off until the user chooses Turn on" reads as if nobody sends before answering.

Is default-on with only a Settings toggle the intended policy? The previous doc said this gate stayed closed "until the privacy policy names Sentry"; the PR says IDP-14 ships separately. If so, I'd make sure IDP-14 merges first (or together), and state the default explicitly in `docs/telemetry.md`.

**Minor — two gates for one decision; the watcher is now dead in production.** Once `daemon.Run` installs `policyCheck`, `policyEnabled` is never read, so the startup seed (`daemon.go:224`) and the 1-second `telemetryPolicy.Watch(..., sentryobs.SetPolicyEnabled)` goroutine (`daemon.go:287`) only update a field nothing consults. The `SetPolicyEnabled` doc comment (line 203: "Capture paths consult it synchronously") is also no longer true.

Also, the "lag" this closes is at most the 1s watcher interval. Options: keep the per-capture check and drop the watcher + `policyEnabled` (and update the comment), or keep the watcher and drop the check. Either way, a single `if check != nil { … } else { … }` reads better than two inverse nil tests.

The new `TestCaptureChecksDurableConsentBetweenWatcherTicks` uses a fake closure, so nothing exercises the real `Reader` as wired in `daemon.Run`.

**Nit — file I/O under the global capture mutex, with no context.** `policyCheck()` does lstat + open + JSON decode while holding `captureGate`, so concurrent captures, `leaveCapture` and `Drain` queue behind disk I/O. I measured ~18µs per check on Windows, so this isn't a real hot-path problem today. But AGENTS.md says I/O functions take `context.Context`, and `CaptureError` already has one. Consider `func(context.Context) bool` and calling the check before taking the lock, re-checking only `active` bookkeeping under it.

**Nit:** the same `telemetryPolicy.EventsAllowed(context.Background(), cfg.Telemetry.Events, cfg.Telemetry.EventsExplicit)` expression is on line 223, here, and again inside `Watch`. One local `eventsAllowedNow := func() bool { … }` would keep the three in sync (or two, if the watcher goes per the `sentryobs.go` comment).

**Nit:** the test name `TestEventsAllowedFollowsTheFileOverTheEnvironment` no longer describes the contract. A missing file now denies, and the environment can veto a consented file (line 99). **Minor (docs):** this reads as if packaged stable/nightly builds send whenever Share error events is on. Fixed in 5424f5d06b. The branch lookup now runs when the worker has no open tracked PR (`!Merged && !Closed`), not only when the list is empty. If only closed or merged PRs are tracked and the lookup finds nothing, the engine now returns the same message with the retry command instead of `no open PR head to review`. New tests: one closed tracked PR plus an open PR on the same branch attaches the open PR and reviews it (service), and a closed-only session gets the retry command (engine).

Fixed in 3d1739faa6. `FindBranchPRs` now looks in the canonical/origin repo and, for a workspace project, in every child repo from `ListWorkspaceRepos` with a parseable origin. These are the same repos `ClaimPR` accepts. Repos are deduplicated, and a child whose provider cannot list by branch (`ErrSCMUnsupported`) is skipped. Any other listing error is still reported as a failed lookup. The session uses the same branch name in each child repo, as the SCM observer does. New test: root plus child repos, PR found in a child repo, unsupported child skipped, failing child named in the error.

Fixed in f58f8d7e4b. `TriggerOptions` has a new `BranchPRLookupFoundNone` field. The service sets it only when `FindBranchPRs` ran and found nothing. The engine says "found no open PR from its branch" only when that field is set. Otherwise (auto-review, a refresher without branch lookup) it says only that AO is not tracking an open PR, plus the retry command. Tests cover both wordings and when the service sets the field.

Fixed in 1d3e4b4cc6. A failed attach now reads `found PR <url> on worker "<id>"'s branch but could not attach it: <cause>; run ao review trigger <id> --pr <url> to try again`. The cause is wrapped, so `ErrNotFound` and the other error classes are unchanged. I wrapped it rather than retrying: if the PR closed in between, a second lookup would just report no PR. New test covers it.

Addressed in f97664da3e. The GitHub adapter has no shared pagination helper; `ListPRsByRepo` pages inline. I added a comment that one page of 100 is deliberate: GitHub allows one open PR per head and base, so with `head=<owner>:<branch>` a second page would need more than 100 base branches.

**Imported chat can start in a folder that doesn't exist in the worktree.** `launchPath` joins `ws.Path` with `source.WorkingSubdir` without checking it exists. `copyImportedWorkspace` only copies what Git reports as changed, so a chat started in a git-ignored or empty folder (e.g. `<repo>/tmp/scratch`), or inside a nested repo the project doesn't register, gets a cwd that is missing in the fresh worktree. The provider then fails with ENOENT on every Retry and the chat never connects. Suggest falling back to `ws.Path` (or creating the folder) when the subdir is missing.

**postCreate runs under the resume request's fixed 10-minute budget.** Native spawns extend their budget with `ports.ExtendSpawnRequestBudget(postCreateBudget(...))`, but resume-agent isn't one of the setup routes that allows that. A project whose postCreate is allowed 20 minutes (e.g. a long dependency install) gets cancelled at 10, `Prepared` is never set, and each Retry or 30-second recheck runs postCreate from the start and is killed again, so the imported chat never opens even though a native spawn of the same project works.

**One record with a different `sessionId` rejects the whole Claude transcript.** Forked or resumed conversations (`--fork-session`, older `claude --resume`) start their new `<id>.jsonl` with copied ancestor records that still carry the old `sessionId`. `readTranscript` errors on the first one, `Scan` skips errors silently, and the chat never appears in the import list. Consider skipping or tolerating ancestor records instead of failing the file. No test covers a Claude transcript with mixed sessionIds.

**Terminated sessions still count as "already imported".** `ListAllSessions` has no `is_terminated` filter, so if the user kills the AO session for an imported chat, the next scan still links the candidate to the dead session: it shows as already in AO with the checkbox disabled, and Import returns `already_imported` pointing at the terminated session. `FindImportedSession` and the `sessions_import_identity` unique index also return or keep the old row, so the chat can never be imported again.

**Import rereads the selected transcripts one at a time while holding `s.mu`.** `Scan` parses these files in parallel with an errgroup, but `Import` decodes each one sequentially (zstd included). With up to 500 selected chats, some of them large, this can pass the 10-minute request budget and leave rows reporting "The import stopped before this conversation". It also blocks any `Scan` from the other agent's tab while it runs. Reading in parallel, as `Scan` does, would make it several times faster.

**`RefreshArchive` walks the whole Codex sessions tree to find one thread.** `discover()` here stats every rollout on each first-open attempt and each 30-second open-elsewhere recheck of a pending Codex import, and `ProbeNativeSession` has already walked the same tree with `findCodexRollout`. A targeted lookup by thread ID, or keeping the segment paths recorded at import time, would avoid both walks for users with thousands of rollouts.

**`ANTHROPIC_MODEL` is now pinned for every Claude ACP launch, not just imported resumes.** This fixes `settings.json` re-applying its model when an imported chat resumes, but the env var now overrides `settings.json` for all Claude chats and is inherited by every tool subprocess the agent runs (a nested `claude -p`, or scripts reading `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, get silently pinned). Suggest limiting the pin to imported or resumed launches.

**Origin matching is case-sensitive and covers only three GitHub URL forms.** A project registered with `git@github.com:Org/Repo.git` and a chat whose clone uses `https://github.com/org/repo` (or `ssh://github.com/Org/Repo`, without `git@`) normalize to different strings, so `lookup()` misses the project and the chat is listed as "<folder> (new project)". Importing it then registers a duplicate project for the same repository. Lowercasing host/owner/repo and handling more URL forms would avoid that.

**`Snapshot()` returns only one page for adopted imports.** For an adopted import with `HistoryThrough > 0`, the full `Snapshot()` now returns `SnapshotPage(ctx, id, 0, 0)`, which is a single default-size page (about 200 rows). Callers that expect the whole history (the controller fallback when the service doesn't implement paging, tests, tools) silently lose older AO turns and the archive, while non-imported sessions still get their full history.

**Unmapped resume failures surface raw error text as a 409.** Errors from `prepareImportedWorkspace` reach the UI verbatim: git stderr, absolute source and provider paths, and postCreate output. Unlike the chat-start path, none of it goes through `agentlaunch.RedactError` with the project env, so a postCreate command that echoes a project env secret could show it in the ControllerBanner. Context-deadline and other server faults are also reported as a conflict rather than a server error.

The pending-approval cap is global across all conversations: each unapproved non-read-only `tools/call` (or `ui/message`) stores one entry, so a single hostile or buggy app can mint 128 pending approvals and keep topping them up as they expire. While it does, `appApproval` refuses new approvals for every other app in every conversation ("too many pending app actions"). Since the design treats apps as untrusted, one app should not be able to disable the approval mechanism for the rest. Scope the cap per conversation or per activity (e.g. count only entries matching `app.ConversationID` here, with a smaller per-scope limit), or evict the oldest pending approval instead of refusing the new one.

This groups a comment that is eligible for injection with its parent review and unconditionally passes `!f.postedByAO(*g.review)` to `writeReviewHeader`, so the parent review body is included even when `review.AutoInjectReview` is false. That is a regression from the previous path, which only injected persisted review bodies from auto-inject-enabled reviews; a comment can remain enabled after its review policy was disabled. Gate the body on the parent review AutoInjectReview as well, while still allowing AO-posted reviews to suppress their summary.

This rewrites a `bun` plan into an `official-installer` plan during execution, after the plan has already been shown and recorded. As a result:
- `displayCommand` (the `UpdateCommand`/`ReinstallCommand` in `AgentPlans`) still shows `bun add @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent ...`, while AO actually downloads and executes a remote shell script from `https://omp.sh/install`. That breaks the transparency the user relies on before approving an install that runs remote code.
- `job.Method` stays `bun` (it comes from `plan.Method` before the call), but `managed.json` now says `official-installer`.
- The interpreter is a bare `"sh"`, while `planShellInstaller` resolves it with `LookPath` and returns an Unsupported plan when it is missing. The URL also duplicates the one in `agentplans.go:240`.

Please move this substitution into the planner, in `planForOperation` where the managed update/reinstall plan is built (for example via `planShellInstaller(TargetOMP, <shared OMP URL>, \"sh\")` + `officialManagedRecipeFor`). Then the displayed command, `Method`, and `UpdateWhileRunning` describe what will actually run, and an unavailable installer surfaces as an Unsupported plan with a reason instead of a failure at run time. Add a test that goes through the planner (`AgentPlans`/update request), not just `runManagedInstall`.

After a successful migration this records `Method: \"official-installer\"`, but OMP's detected plan is still `bun`. The reinstall path in `agentplans.go` (`planForOperation`) only repairs AO's managed copy when `record.Method == plan.Method`. After a migration that check fails, so a Reinstall skips the managed copy and falls through to the regular `bun` reinstall of the user's system copy: exactly the Bun runtime path this PR avoids. The managed release sessions actually run is not repaired.

Please make the reinstall/update gate recognize a migrated OMP record (or treat a migrated record as owned by the bun plan for OMP on darwin/linux). Add a regression test that runs a reinstall after a migration and asserts it reinstalls the managed standalone release with `--binary --ref <record.Version>`.

OMP is a Pi fork, so a session file is a tree: each entry has `id`/`parentId`, and rewinding or branching inside a session appends new entries under an earlier parent in the same file. This loop adds every user/assistant message in file order. An imported chat would then show abandoned branches mixed in with the active one, such as a rewound prompt followed by its replacement. The Claude path already handles this problem by walking from the leaf through `parentUuid` (see `transcript.go`, around "Follow the active branch so rewound prompts are not shown as history"). OpenCode marks text parts it injects itself with `"synthetic": true`. An `@file` attachment, for example, becomes a synthetic text part that echoes the Read tool call and the file contents into the user message, and some injected parts are also marked `"ignored": true`. OpenCode's own UI hides these, but this query keeps every `type = 'text'` part. Imported user turns would then show whole file bodies and tool-call boilerplate the user never typed, and that text also counts against the visible-byte budget and can become the fallback title. Filter them out, e.g. `AND COALESCE(json_extract(data, '$.synthetic'), 0) = 0 AND COALESCE(json_extract(data, '$.ignored'), 0) = 0`, and add a fixture case with a synthetic part on a user message to `TestOpenCodeTranscriptKeepsOnlyUserAssistantText`.

**The Pi open-elsewhere check can never detect a live Pi writer.** Pi does not hold its session file open. In `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` `dist/core/session-manager.js`, `_persist` calls `appendFileSync(this.sessionFile, ...)` for each entry, and `_rewriteFile` calls `writeFileSync`. Both open, write and close the file right away. So `lsof -F pcfa -- <transcript>` only reports a Pi process during the instant of a write, and `processRunsPi`/`identifiesPi` are effectively never reached for a real Pi session.

**Result:** importing a conversation that is still open in the Pi CLI/TUI is not refused. After the resume, AO's pi-acp and the other Pi process both append to the same file under their own in-memory leaf, which interleaves branches in the tree. The PR description also says that, without lsof, the provider refuses a second writer. pi-acp does not: `session/load` opens the file and keeps appending.

**Required:** find a live Pi owner by something Pi actually keeps. For example, scan for running processes that `identifiesPi` accepts, then match one to this session by its argv (`--session <id or path>`) or by its cwd (`lsof -a -d cwd -p <pid>`) equal to the transcript header's cwd, the same way `claudeSessionLive` skips AO's own workspace. If no reliable signal exists, drop the Pi lsof/argv probe and its tests. Then state in the code and in the PR that Pi has no open-elsewhere protection, instead of shipping a check that looks protective but never fires.

**`context.clear` / `context.undo` are not honored, so the imported history includes retracted turns.**

Kimi Code 2.3.3 writes both records to `wire.jsonl` as durable events. Its own transcript rebuild resets on `context.clear` (`clearFloor = transcript.length`) and folds back on `context.undo` (`applyUndo(record.count)`). Its context-recovery prompt also tells the model: *"`context.undo` count=N retracts the previous N messages, treat retracted content as never having happened. `context.clear` resets the conversation."*

This switch drops both records, so:
- a user who ran `/clear` and started over imports the whole pre-clear conversation, and `kimiTitle`'s prompt fallback can pick a pre-clear prompt;
- undone prompts/replies still appear in the imported history;
- the history AO shows differs from what `session/load` actually restores.

Fix: on `context.clear`, flush and then reset `items` (and `prompted`). On `context.undo`, flush and drop the last `count` user-prompt turns, meaning each user prompt together with the assistant text that follows it, which matches Kimi's undo-anchor semantics for typed prompts. Add fixtures for both cases.

**Kimi open-elsewhere detection is very likely to never trigger, at least on macOS.**

This guard depends on lsof reporting a writable fd held by a process whose command contains `kimi`. Two things go against that:
- `kimi` is a Node script (`/opt/homebrew/Cellar/kimi-code/2.3.3/bin/kimi` starts with `#!/opt/homebrew/opt/node/bin/node`). Kimi sets `process.title = "kimi-code"`, but on Darwin libuv does not change the kernel `p_comm` that lsof's `c` field reports, so the command shows as `node` and `strings.Contains(command, "kimi")` (L229) does not match. Linux may differ because libuv uses `prctl` there.
- Kimi's host FS `appendText` uses `fs.appendFile` (open, append, close per call), so a running Kimi probably does not keep `wire.jsonl` open between records. Even with the right name, lsof would almost always find no writer.

The result: an imported Kimi chat that is still open in the user's terminal can be resumed by AO at the same time, with two writers appending to the same `wire.jsonl`. That is the situation `ErrSessionOpenElsewhere` exists to prevent.

Please either find a real liveness signal (for example, look for a Kimi process whose argv carries `--session <id>`/`acp` and whose cwd or home matches, or any lock/registry Kimi keeps), or, if none exists, say plainly in the code and the PR that Kimi has no open-elsewhere protection rather than implying it. Whichever you choose, add a test of the matching logic (for example, the lsof `-F pcfa` parsing with a `cnode` process line).

You're right — Pi persists with appendFileSync/writeFileSync, so lsof never catches it, and pi-acp's session/load doesn't refuse a second writer. A reliable per-session signal doesn't exist either (argv `--session <id>` only appears on a *resumed* TUI, missing the original still-open session; cwd equality is ambiguous across sibling sessions in one folder). So I took the "drop it" option: removed the Pi lsof/argv probe and its tests, reverted writableTranscriptOwner to the Claude/Codex form, and documented in both importOwnedElsewhere and writableTranscriptOwner (and the PR body) that Pi has no open-elsewhere protection. Fixed in 77eff17690.

**Undo anchor parity with Kimi is incomplete, so AO removes different turns than Kimi restores.**

Kimi Code 2.3.3's `applyUndo` walks back from the end. It skips `injection` messages, stops at a `compaction_summary`, and counts a message as an undo anchor (`isUndoAnchor`) when it has `role == "user"` and one of these is true:
- `origin` is missing, or `origin.kind == "user"` without `origin.inTurn == true`, or
- `origin.kind` is `skill_activation` or `plugin_command` with `origin.trigger == "user-slash"`.

`dropLastKimiTurns` instead counts the visible user items, which are exactly the `origin.kind == "user"` messages kept at L202. That diverges in four cases:
- **User-slash skill or plugin command:** the user runs `/review`, then undoes once. Kimi retracts the skill turn. AO dropped that skill message at L202, so it retracts the previous typed prompt instead, together with the skill's reply that was merged into it. AO removes too much.
- **In-turn steer** (`kind:"user", inTurn:true`): Kimi does not count it as an anchor, but AO does, so AO removes too little.
- **Prompt with no origin:** Kimi counts it (`origin === undefined`), but L202 drops it entirely. That also hides the message from the imported history.
- **Compaction:** Kimi never undoes past a `context.apply_compaction`, but AO does.

Fix: track undo anchors separately from what is displayed. For example, keep a hidden anchor marker in `items` for each Kimi anchor (including user-slash skill and plugin activations, which stay hidden), let `dropLastKimiTurns` count markers and stop at a compaction boundary, and strip the markers before building `t.messages`. Also accept origin-less user messages as typed prompts at L202. Add fixtures for the user-slash skill + undo case and the `inTurn` case.

That means `strings.Contains(command, "kimi")` at L229 does not match. Kimi also writes records through `fs.appendFile` (open, append, close each time), so normally no writable descriptor stays open for lsof to see.

As things stand, AO can resume an imported Kimi chat that is still open in the user's terminal, and both processes will append to the same `wire.jsonl`. **A typed prompt with no visible text loses its undo anchor, so undo counts drift from Kimi.**

This branch adds the item only when `visibleText` is non-empty. But Kimi's `isUndoAnchor` depends only on role and origin, not on content. Example: `task A` → reply, then an image-only prompt → reply, then `context.undo count=1`. Kimi retracts the image turn and keeps `task A`. AO finds `task A` as the last anchor and drops it along with both replies.

**Cloud PDF cards re-download the whole file every ~8 minutes.** Access prefixes expire after 10 min (`artifactAccessTTL` on the control plane), and `useCloudArtifactAccess` renews them 2 min early. Each renewal is a new token, so `contentUrl` changes here. Cards aren't pinned, so `PdfPreview`'s `src` changes, its effect re-runs, and every visible cloud PDF card fetches the full file through the main process again (up to 100 MiB), re-parses it with pdf.js, and flashes "Loading…" meanwhile. With the 4-live-preview budget that's up to 4 full downloads per renewal, plus on window focus near expiry.

Image and HTML cards also reload on renewal, but a PDF costs much more. Could the card pin its URL the way the viewer does (`usePinnedArtifactUrl`, repin on failure), or key the load on path + `updatedAt` instead of the full URL?

**A failed cloud PDF card never asks for a fresh link.** `onError` only sets `failed`, while cloud images (via the HEAD status check) and HTML cards (`CloudArtifactFrame onAccessRefused`) call `refreshAccess()` on a refusal. If the prefix has expired (e.g. after sleep, when the refetch timer was throttled), the card shows the placeholder until the next scheduled renewal changes `contentUrl`. The PR's "one fresh access link, then Retry" only holds for the viewer.

Suggest:
```tsx
onError={() => { setFailed(true); if (cloud) refreshAccess(); }}
```
`refreshAccess` already limits itself to one refresh per file version. A test alongside the new thumbnail test would be good too.

- The IPC read can't be cancelled. If the user opens a large cloud PDF and switches files, the main process keeps downloading and still sends the full buffer to the renderer, which drops it. Not blocking, but worth a follow-up if large cloud PDFs are common.

**P2: on iOS, the window catches transcript scrolling.**

**P2: Card previews inline the full page into JS memory.**

Each visible HTML card calls `useInlinedArtifactPage`, which reads every linked image (up to 10 MiB each, 25 MiB per page) into a base64 string. `artifactPageCache` keeps up to 12 of these strings, `thumbnailPageHtml` makes another copy, and the bridge copies it again into the native WebView. Chat frames take the same path.

A gallery of screenshot-heavy reports on a low-memory Android phone can run out of memory. The self-review lists this as optional. I think it should block, because the failure is a crash, not a slow screen.

Suggested fix:
- Use a small budget for cards: skip images over ~300 KB, or skip images in thumbnails entirely.
- Cap `artifactPageCache` by total size, not by entry count.

**P2: PDFs open to a blank screen on Android.**

`.pdf` is in `WEB_MEDIA`, so the viewer loads it in a WebView. Android's WebView has no built-in PDF renderer. It shows nothing, or starts a download that has no auth header. iOS works.

Suggested fix: on Android, treat PDF like an unknown file (icon plus "Open it on the machine"). Or download it to a temp file and hand it to the system viewer.

**P2: Up to 1 MiB of text goes into one selectable `<Text>`.**

`MAX_ARTIFACT_TEXT_BYTES` is 1 MiB, and highlighting turns off only above 100 KB. So a 900 KB log, CSV or JSON file becomes one Android TextView inside a ScrollView that is not virtualized. Android lays out the whole string on the UI thread. At this size that usually means freezes of several seconds, and it can trigger an ANR. A large markdown file in `ChatMarkdown` with `continuousSelection` has the same problem.

Suggested fix: use a much lower in-app cap (for example 200 KB), and let larger files fall back to the daemon page, as files over 1 MiB already do. Or show the first N lines with a "Showing the start" note, like the version screen does.

Two effects: - JS like `const srcset = "a.png 1x";` loses ` srcset = "a.png 1x"` and becomes `const;`. That is a syntax error and kills the whole script. - Template strings like `''` start a fetch for `${url}`. Suggested fix: run the image and srcset passes before inlining scripts and stylesheets, or skip `

**P3: Linked files are fetched one at a time.**

`replaceAsync` awaits each match in order. A page with 10 images makes 10 round trips in series. Over a cloudflared or Tailscale link, every chat frame and gallery card waits on this.

Suggested fix: start all loads first, then splice in the results (`Promise.all` over the matches). For dedupe to keep working while loads run at the same time, the `images` map in `inlineArtifactPage` must store the promise, not the result.

**P3: Unknown extensions count as text, so binary files get Copy and Version history.**

`artifactViewKind` falls back to `"text"`, and `canCopyArtifact` and `canShowArtifactHistory` follow it. So a `.zip`, `.docx`, `.xlsx` or `.sqlite` artifact shows both actions:
- Copy downloads the file, then fails.
- History lists versions, but `GET artifact-versions/{n}` returns `ARTIFACT_FILE_BINARY`. The version screen shows an error and never offers Restore.

On desktop, History is hidden when the file read reports `binary`. Suggested fix: decide these actions from a list of text extensions, or from the `looksBinary` result once the file has been read.

**P2: the Worker row can keep a stale live status for the whole app run.**

`readSession` caches its first answer per session until the app restarts. It was written for names, which do not change. This row uses it for status and for the Open/Restore choice.

How to hit it on a daemon that pages its archive:
1. Cold start from a review notification. The PR page mounts before the first poll lands, so `sessions` is `[]` and `listed` is false.
2. `readSession` reads the worker while it is live, and caches that snapshot.
3. The poll lands, the worker is listed, and the row looks right.
4. Later in the same run the worker is archived (for example after the PR merges). It drops out of the poll, `listed` turns false, and the effect gets the cached live snapshot back.

The row then shows the old live status and **Open** instead of **Restore**. `autoReviewEnabled` also comes from that stale copy, so the 2s review poll keeps running for an archived worker.

Suggested fix: call `getSession(config, sessionId)` directly here (this page reads one session, so the shared cache gives nothing), or delete the cache entry after a read that is not terminated.

[P2] Report terminal kills when subsequent cleanup fails

This call is skipped whenever manager.Kill returns an error, even if the session is already durably terminated. Manager.kill calls recordTermination before runPreRemove, so a failing cleanup command is a concrete case where termination succeeds and Kill then returns an error. No ao.sessions.ended event is emitted, and a later retry sees IsTerminated and sets live=false, permanently losing the outcome. Check whether termination committed on the error path and report it using the saved pre-termination record, as the replacement path already does. Apply the same handling to RequestKill and lifecycle completion teardown where errors can follow terminal persistence, and cover a post-termination cleanup failure in a regression.

[P2] Avoid counting replayed steer requests as new messages

Svc.Steer returns a successful stored receipt when the same clientMessageId is replayed; Controller.steerLocked explicitly returns replaySteerDelivery without contacting the provider again. This unconditional increment therefore counts every retry of one accepted human steer, inflating steer_count and the surface counter, including retries after a daemon restart. The existing TestSteerIsIdempotentOnTheClientHandle already demonstrates that successful replay behavior. Count at the durable acceptance boundary or propagate a duplicate result so this controller increments only for a newly accepted steer, and add a counter regression for two requests using the same handle.

[P2] Verify the selected code before restoring a live selection

Intended behavior when opening a saved code snippet:
- If the file/code has changed, open the file without highlighting the captured snippet.
- If it is unchanged, open the file and highlight the original snippet.

This PR preserves that opening behavior: `SessionView` omits `annotationRange` for a `changed` resolution, and `useFileAnnotationReveal` checks the captured text before highlighting. This finding is about a separate interaction: keeping an active mouse selection alive during a live refresh.

`restoreCodeSelection` resolves both endpoints using `rows[end.rowIndex]` and character offsets, without checking that the replacement rows still contain the selected code. If a refresh inserts or removes displayed rows before the selection while retaining the column, the same indexes now identify different code. The PR restores the highlight there, and Add to chat can capture that different code.

Reproduction: select two rows containing `original();` and `selected();`, then rebuild the column with `inserted();` before those rows. The restored endpoints move onto `inserted();` and `original();`; invoking the hook's `ask()` passes those rows to the callback. I reproduced this with an isolated jsdom hook test against commit 4ca0ddf9e1667f7bac052249853502731c6efcbf. The 38 existing selection/reveal unit tests and two added reproduction tests passed; Electron and end-to-end tests were not run.

Please verify the captured row identity/content before restoring. If the original snippet cannot be safely matched, leave the file open and clear the active selection instead of highlighting or quoting unrelated code. The current redraw tests clone identical rows, so they do not cover this content-changing refresh.

[P2] Preserve the request ID across an uncertain start

If the daemon commits the worker but its response is lost, the catch leaves this suggestion available and a second Start generates a different UUID. The daemon therefore creates another worker for the same task instead of replaying the first result. Keep the request ID and submitted payload for each unresolved suggestion and reuse them on retry; add coverage for a committed start whose first response is lost.

It also reappears after refetch because the delegate request carries only brief text and DelegateTask never sets the session IssueID, which issueNumbersInProject relies on. [P2] Bind the modifier intent to an actual submission

This callback runs before submit checks whether a message can be sent. For example, Cmd/Ctrl+Enter on an empty new-task composer sets NewChatPage.startNextRef, but performClaimedSubmit returns without calling onSend, so the flag is never consumed. Typing a task and pressing plain Enter afterward unexpectedly keeps the page open and labels the spawn composer_next. The same stale flag can occur when submit joins an existing in-flight send. Carry the modifier with the accepted delivery, or clear it when that submission does not reach onSend, and cover the empty-submit case.

An active -> idle transition is also emitted when work fails or the user stops it: Claude `stop-failure` maps to idle, `observe/activity/turn_failures.go` sends idle for both turn errors and interrupts, and Chat sends idle for `chat.interrupt.reconciled`. This helper therefore creates an `agent_completed` notification saying "Your agent finished its work and is ready for review" after, for example, an API rate-limit failure or pressing Stop before a result exists. Preserve the outcome/event when deciding whether to emit this notification, and either suppress these cases or give them appropriate failure/interruption copy. Cover those transitions alongside the successful-turn test.

**Switching the client changes the account ID of everyone signed in today, and their next sign-in removes and re-imports all their account machines.**

WorkOS user IDs are per environment. The control plane links old and new users through `external_id`, but mobile keys everything on the WorkOS `user.id`. So the ID returned by the production client is not the ID stored now. For a user signed in today:

1. Refreshing the old-environment token fails. `refreshAccountToken` then calls `signOutOfAccount()`, and the background sync in `lib/store.tsx` swallows the error. Account machines stay in the host list with `accountUserId` set to the old ID, because only the Settings Sign out button calls `clearAccountHosts()`.
2. They sign in again and get a new ID. Before re-adding the listing, `performSync` in `lib/accountHosts.ts` forgets every host whose `accountUserId !== account.id`. For each account machine that queues a push unpair (`unpairFromServer`), clears its chat event cursors and deletes the record. The re-add then finds no `existing` record, so the name and icon the user picked on the phone are lost. Machines the user hid with Forget come back, because `ao.accountHosts.ignored.<id>` is keyed by the old ID.

Please make the switch keep the user’s machines. For example:
- When a stored host has a different `accountUserId` but the new account’s listing still contains it, update `accountUserId` in place, keeping name, appearance and endpoints, instead of forgetting it.
- Move the hidden-machine set from the old ID to the new one. Keep the legacy session’s ID when you discard it, so it is still known at the next sign-in.

Storing the issuing client ID with the session would let you recognize a legacy session directly, instead of depending on WorkOS answering `invalid_grant`. Any other error leaves the old account looking signed in while every sync fails.

Add a test for the migration: hosts tagged with the old ID, plus a new-account listing that still contains them, end up with their phone-local names and appearance kept and no unpair queued.

A test would be: inspect, modify the file, publish, and assert nothing was uploaded.

**Blocker: New Chat now treats every daemon refusal as an uncertain send.**

This drops the typed `TaskCreateError` (its `name` and `code`), and `sendIsUncertain` in `NewChatPage.tsx:469-472` depends on it. With a plain `Error` and no `code`, it returns `true` for every refusal:

2. The retry reuses that ID, so `send` reads the saved pending launch and sends `saved.replay`, which still carries the original agent, model and effort.

Example: in New Chat, `UNSUPPORTED_MODEL` → "The agent default is selected. Review it and start again" → the retry resends the unsupported model and fails the same way. The same happens for `AGENT_BINARY_NOT_FOUND`, `BRANCH_CHECKED_OUT_ELSEWHERE`, `AGENT_AUTH_REQUIRED` and the rest, and `refusedRetry` can no longer appear.

Verified by running `sendIsUncertain` (copied verbatim) on both throws: `new TaskCreateError("...", "UNSUPPORTED_MODEL")` gives `false` (main), and `new Error(message)` gives `true` (this PR). The NewChatPage tests can't catch this. They mock `useTaskLaunch`, and the new ones reject with a plain `Error`, while the existing ones model refusals as `{ name: "TaskCreateError", code }`.

Suggested fix:
```ts
throw err instanceof TaskCreateError
	? new TaskCreateError(message, err.code, err.details)
	: err instanceof Error ? err : new Error(message);
```

I replayed the git commands `Resolve`/`Inspect` run, in temp repos:
- **Remoteless repo, main checkout on `feature/wip`:** a new task's base resolves to `refs/heads/feature/wip`. After `git switch main`, it resolves to `refs/heads/main`. The project's reported `defaultBranch` (`projectFromRow` → `Inspect`) follows the checkout the same way.

[P1] Resolve AO-managed launchers through to the underlying npm target

AO-managed installs pass an extra wrapper here: `systeminstall.ensureManagedLauncher` (`backend/internal/service/systeminstall/managed.go:532-535`) writes `@"%~dp0..\cline\current\cline.cmd" %*`, and `binaryutil.ManagedBinary` is preferred over PATH. This wrapper is not bypassed: the tokenizer keeps the leading `@` in the program token, so the existence check fails and the original `.cmd` argv is returned. Merely stripping `@` would still leave the nested npm `.cmd` as the executable because the resolver only unwraps one level.

Consequently, Cline installed/updated through AO still sends the generated system prompt through cmd.exe and retains the original command-line-length failure. This affects worker and reviewer launch paths that use that managed launcher.

I reproduced the resolver gap on Windows at `97567a8bc` with a temporary fixture matching the installer's exact wrapper shape and a 13,000-character prompt: the underlying npm shim resolves to `node.exe <entry>`, but the managed launcher remains `bin\cline.cmd`. The existing shim and reviewer regression tests pass, so they do not catch this case.

Please unwrap the known AO-managed launcher through to a directly launchable target, with a bounded/cycle-safe traversal, and add a regression using the managed-launcher shape as well as the direct npm shim.

[P2] Extend the takeover wait with the shutdown budget

Installer draining now allows 284 seconds, but `lockDataDir` still gives a replacement daemon only 108 seconds to acquire the data-directory lock (`daemon.go:193`). Desktop takeover starts the replacement when `/healthz` disappears, while the old process continues cleanup. One stalled 120-second cleanup command can therefore make the replacement exit 75; its exit handler leaves the app stopped without retrying. A scaled lock regression reproduced the refusal. Derive the takeover wait from the expanded shutdown budget.

[P2] Prevent a second automatic SIGTERM from killing restoration

Restart disposes the supervisor link and sends SIGTERM (`frontend/src/main.ts:2502-2509`). The `stop()` call above removes the daemon's signal handler before cleanup finishes. If the user quits Electron during cleanup, its disconnected-link exit fallback sends another SIGTERM (`frontend/src/main.ts:3792-3794`), terminating the daemon before `brew link opencode` runs. A subprocess regression reproduced this termination. Suppress the fallback for an already-stopping daemon, or retain signal handling through restoration.

**[P2] Restore exclusion for authentication terminals surviving daemon restart**

This lookup only knows terminals created by the current agent-auth service:

1. Start a terminal login.
2. Restart the daemon within the same Electron app launch; `AO_APP_RUN_ID` stays the same.
3. Shellterm deliberately retains current-app command terminals, but the new service initializes `terminalLogins` empty.
4. Start a background login: it skips the liveness probe and can write to the same credentials while the old terminal login is still running.

A fresh-service reproduction accepted the background login with the retained terminal alive and zero liveness probes. The survival behavior is also covered by `TestCommandTerminalLifetimeAcrossRestarts`. Reconcile ownership of surviving authentication terminals before admitting another login.

**[P2] Retain update exclusion after failed cancellation**

This `finally` releases the guard even when disposal failed:

1. Start inline sign-in on a remote host.
2. Disconnect the host; `disconnectHost` removes its client before the panel unmounts.
3. Cleanup cannot look up that client, so cancellation rejects without sending DELETE; this block then clears the pending state.
4. Reconnect: Update becomes available and can send an install request while the native login is still running.

A component integration reproduction using the real host lookup, disconnect/reconnect, and lifecycle code confirmed zero cancellation requests followed by an install request. Retain the outstanding operation after failed disposal and retry cancellation or reconcile its state after reconnect before allowing updates.

**[P3] Apply the remote Codex restriction to automatic browser opening**

1. A Codex browser-login operation is already running on the remote daemon.
2. The remote user selects Device code; `startAgentUILogin` recovers the existing browser operation through `AGENT_AUTH_IN_PROGRESS`.
3. This effect opens its OAuth URL on the local machine, where the localhost callback cannot reach the remote CLI.

The manual Open sign-in page button already excludes this remote/browser combination, but the new automatic effect does not. Apply the same exclusion here, or reject incompatible recovery. A component reproduction confirmed automatic opening while the manual link remained hidden.

[P1] Enforce the local-only tool boundary before starting inference

`unsafe_dynamic_tools` adds AO's tools; it does not replace Coder's built-ins. In the pinned [v2.37.9 implementation](https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/v2.37.9/coderd/x/chatd/chatd.go#L3845-L3955), `appendRootChatTools` still exposes `create_workspace`, `start_workspace`, `stop_workspace` and subagent tools, and `appendDynamicTools` appends the client tools afterward. Those built-ins execute on the server without an AO approval. The model can invoke one immediately after this POST, even before `pump` connects; `mapEvent`/`failClosed` observes the tool call asynchronously and cannot guarantee interruption before its side effects. Thus ask-first and read-only conversations can provision or act on a remote workspace despite the local-only contract. Require a server-enforced local-only tool configuration/contract before sending the first prompt, or reject configurations whose guarantees cannot be enforced; detecting a workspace binding after the turn is too late.

A `waiting` chat also gets no adopted turn. `pump` then connects with `after_id` at that maximum, so the server excludes the missed reply permanently. This conversation does not implement `ports.ChatHistoryReader`, so the service's native-history import cannot recover it either. Reconcile provider history against AO's durable projection (with stable message/turn identities), or persist and resume from the last actually projected cursor. Add a regression covering detach during a run, server-side completion, then resume and recovery of the final assistant reply.

[P1] Background tasks leave a persistent Coder chat behind after every turn

After each completed turn, `SessionChatSurface` asks for a prompt suggestion. There is no harness gate on that path: `RunPromptSuggestionTask` calls `RunBackgroundTask`, and so does the delegated-title path. `RunBackgroundTask` calls `Start` with `Ephemeral: true` and `DisableTools: true`, and then `Terminate`.

This driver drops `Ephemeral`, and the conversation has no archive or delete call. `Terminate` only interrupts while a turn is still active, and by then the turn has completed. So each suggestion:
- reconnects (`Me`, organizations, models),
- creates a new chat labelled `ao.session=background-…` that carries the recent transcript,
- spends model quota,
- stays in the user's Coder chat list for good.

I checked this with a probe on the PR's `fakeCoder`: Start with `Ephemeral`, `ReadOnly` and `DisableTools`, one turn, then `Terminate`. The chat was still there, `archived=false`, `interrupts=0`.

Suggested fix: honor `cfg.Ephemeral` by archiving or deleting the chat in `Terminate`/`Close`, if Coder's chats API supports that. If it doesn't, have the driver reject `Ephemeral` starts so these optional features fall back cleanly instead of writing to the deployment. Please add a regression test for whichever you choose.

Most records are cut down to `{state: submitted}`. But a call that reached `done` and was never submitted (submit failed, AO stopped, or the chat ended) keeps the full tool output indefinitely. That output can be file contents or command output.

**[P1] Switching Claude sign-in leaves its API-key override enabled**

Save an Anthropic key from Claude's panel, then select Setup token or complete subscription sign-in. The harness claim remains, so subsequent sessions still receive `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. For setup tokens, `AugmentRuntimeEnv` returns immediately upon seeing that key, before loading the newly saved token. A successful subscription login likewise only removes the saved setup token, leaving the API-key override active.

**Fix:** Revoke Claude's key claim after successfully selecting another sign-in method, while retaining the shared key for other harnesses.

**[P1] Startup discards user-exported credentials**

If AO has an OpenAI key saved for another harness, starting AO with a different user-exported `OPENAI_API_KEY` overwrites that exported value here. Codex's launch then blanks the saved value because Codex has no claim: `runtimeEnvChecked` sees that the daemon environment equals the stored key. The explicitly exported credential is lost, contrary to the documented behavior.

**Fix:** Preserve the inherited environment separately from AO's probe credentials and use that original value when constructing session environments.

**[P1] Stale model requests can configure the wrong provider**

In Qwen's panel, start loading OpenAI models, then switch to Anthropic before the response arrives. Switching remains enabled because `loadingModels` is excluded from `locked`, and this response only checks whether the component is mounted. It populates Anthropic's picker with OpenAI models and can automatically select one; saving then writes an unusable provider/model combination.

**Fix:** Cancel or ignore model responses when the selected method or credential changes.

**[P2] Gemini key saves reject valid commented settings**

The writer uses plain `json.Unmarshal`, so a valid Gemini settings file containing comments produces `AGENT_AUTH_STORE_INVALID`. The existing Gemini probe explicitly supports those comments through `stripGeminiJSONComments`. This affects users with commented settings, so it is non-blocking.

**Fix:** Use comment-aware decoding consistent with the probe.

**pnpm shims lose their environment (P2).** pnpm's cmd-shim runs `@SET "NODE_PATH=<store>\node_modules"` inside `@SETLOCAL` before the `%*` line. Only the `%*` line is parsed here, so the unwrapped child starts without `NODE_PATH`. With a pnpm-shaped fixture, the entry printed `NODE_PATH=undefined`. Through the shim it would get the store path. Global CLIs that rely on pnpm's NODE_PATH resolution can then fail to load their dependencies.

The comments at L13/L82 claim pnpm support, but there's no pnpm fixture in the tests. Suggestion: decline to unwrap a shim that `SET`s anything other than `dp0`/`_prog`/`PATHEXT`, or carry those variables into `cmd.Env`. Either way, add a pnpm fixture.

Yarn v1 global bins, for example, chain to `...\Data\global\node_modules\.bin\<tool>.cmd`. Nit/perf: this adds a full `exec.LookPath` (a PATH × PATHEXT stat scan) to every `process.Command` and `CommandContext` call daemon-wide, including git hot paths, and `exec.Command` then repeats the same lookup. Through `systemexec` it runs three times. Shims are also re-stat'd and re-read on every launch.

Cheaper option: build the `exec.Cmd` first, check `isBatchFile(cmd.Path)` (exec.Command has already resolved it), and only then rewrite `cmd.Path`/`cmd.Args`.

Nit: the comment says the unfamiliar shim "keeps its previous cmd.exe path", but the test asserts `cmd.Path == shim`, which means Go's default batch launch, not an explicit cmd.exe line. It also runs from `t.TempDir()`, which has no spaces, so it can't catch the spaced-path failure described on `systemexec/process_windows.go`.
